source_snapshot.title: Urban Planning Committee, RTA and Dubai Municipality launch new addressing identity
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 7th October, 2026 (WAM) -- The Supreme Committee for Urban Planning, in coordination with Dubai’s Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) and Dubai Municipality, has launched a new visual identity and enhanced addressing system for areas across the Emirate of Dubai. The initiative includes the installation and replacement of area identification signs, internal street name signs, and house number plates, featuring unified designs and colours that reflect the geographic characteristics of each area.Developed through a specialist consultant in wayfinding and addressing design, the new system will help facilitate the identification of locations and improve accessibility, while enhancing the visual appeal of streets, residential neighbourhoods, and commercial districts.The launch forms part of efforts to establish an integrated and clear addressing system that keeps pace with Dubai’s rapid urban development. Going beyond its traditional wayfinding role, the new system is designed to become an integral component of the visual identity of Dubai’s areas, while contributing to the enhancement of streets and road facilities and highlighting the geographic and urban characteristics that distinguish communities across the emirate.The implementation plan covers 186 areas distributed across 19 sectors throughout Dubai, under a phased programme that will begin in the fourth quarter of 2026 and continue through 2030. The first phase of the project will commence this year and will include the installation and replacement of more than 2,000 signs across five areas: Za’abeel 1, Za’abeel 2, Nad Al Sheba, Al Khawaneej 1, and Nazwa, in accordance with the approved visual identity for each area.The new visual identity incorporates five colours specifically designed to reflect the character and geographic features of Dubai’s various areas, providing each with a distinctive visual signature while maintaining a clear and consistent addressing system across the emirate. The selected colours have been carefully aligned with the nature of each area. For example, blue represents areas located close to the sea, while gold symbolises areas characterised by a desert environment, reflecting the diversity of Dubai’s landscapes and urban fabric.The new identity encompasses sector and area identification signs, internal street name signs, and house number plates, with designs and colour schemes developed to achieve visual integration across all components of the addressing system. Future project deliverables will extend the identity to bus stops, smart applications, and area map boards. In addition, QR codes will be introduced to provide information about sectors and areas, the meanings behind street and area names, points of interest, and other relevant location-related content.In coordination with Dubai Municipality, RTA has established a set of criteria to determine implementation priorities across the emirate. These include urban growth and population density, the vibrancy and centrality of areas, the presence of residential and tourist attractions, and the proportion of streets that have not yet been formally addressed. This approach ensures that project implementation aligns with urban development trends and the needs of residents across Dubai.As part of the continued rollout of the new addressing identity, RTA has coordinated with Dubai Municipality to complete and approve the final designs for house number plates. These plates will feature each property's Makani number and corresponding QR Code, with colours harmonised with those of the new addressing signs to enhance visual integration, reinforce a unified identity, and further facilitate location identification.

source_snapshot.title: Theyab bin Tahnoon inaugurates 15th season of Dubai Miracle Garden
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 8th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Sheikh Theyab bin Tahnoon bin Mohammed Al Nahyan, Chairman of Miracle Group, today inaugurated the 15th season of Dubai Miracle Garden, the world’s largest natural flower garden, under the theme ‘Fifteen Years, Blooming Together’.Running until 31st May 2027, the new season features more than 200 million flowers across 72,000 square metres and, for the first time, will introduce a new theme each week throughout the season.The inauguration was attended by Hamdan Al Kaabi, Vice Chairman of Miracle Group; Eng. Mohammed Zaher Hammadih, Group CEO of Miracle Group; senior executives of the Group; and representatives from Dubai’s tourism and hospitality sectors.Sheikh Theyab bin Tahnoon bin Mohammed Al Nahyan highlighted the ongoing efforts to enhance Dubai Miracle Garden’s appeal as one of Dubai’s leading attractions, distinguished by its unique floral displays and creative designs.He said, “Over its fifteen seasons, Dubai Miracle Garden has grown alongside Dubai, becoming part of the memories of its residents and visitors. This season is dedicated to the community that has contributed to its success, particularly the families and residents who continue to return year after year.”The weekly themes will reflect the national and cultural calendar, bringing the UAE’s diverse communities together through flowers, art and music.The opening months of the season will focus on wellness, culture and community, with activities marking Pink October, United Nations Day, UAE Flag Day and Diwali. The programme will also feature live music, family activities and fitness events as part of the Dubai Fitness Challenge. Dedicated events will also mark Commemoration Day and Eid Al Etihad.Eng. Mohammed Zaher Hammadih said, “As we mark our 15th season, Dubai Miracle Garden continues to bring people together through shared experiences. Our weekly programme gives families a new reason to return, with cultural celebrations, live entertainment and activities to enjoy throughout the season.”The garden showcases more than 150 flower varieties alongside its signature floral structures, which have earned it multiple Guinness World Records.Since opening in 2013, Dubai Miracle Garden has welcomed millions of visitors and established itself as one of the region’s leading family attractions, contributing to Dubai’s appeal as a global tourism destination.Dubai Miracle Garden will welcome visitors daily from 8 October 2026 to 31st May 2027. Opening hours are from 9am to 9pm on weekdays and from 9am to 11pm on weekends. Entry is free for children under the age of three.

DUBAI, 8th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Sheikh Theyab bin Tahnoon bin Mohammed Al Nahyan, Chairman of Miracle Group, today inaugurated the 15th season of Dubai Miracle Garden, the world’s largest natural flower garden, under the theme ‘Fifteen Years, Blooming Together’.Running until 31st May 2027, the new season features more than 200 million flowers across 72,000 square metres and, for the first time, will introduce a new theme each week throughout the season.The inauguration was attended by Hamdan Al Kaabi, Vice Chairman of Miracle Group; Eng.

Mohammed Zaher Hammadih, Group CEO of Miracle Group; senior executives of the Group; and representatives from Dubai’s tourism and hospitality sectors.Sheikh Theyab bin Tahnoon bin Mohammed Al Nahyan highlighted the ongoing efforts to enhance Dubai Miracle Garden’s appeal as one of Dubai’s leading attractions, distinguished by its unique floral displays and creative designs.He said, “Over its fifteen seasons, Dubai Miracle Garden has grown alongside Dubai, becoming part of the memories of its residents and visitors.

This season is dedicated to the community that has contributed to its success, particularly the families and residents who continue to return year after year.”The weekly themes will reflect the national and cultural calendar, bringing the UAE’s diverse communities together through flowers, art and music.The opening months of the season will focus on wellness, culture and community, with activities marking Pink October, United Nations Day, UAE Flag Day and Diwali.
The programme will also feature live music, family activities and fitness events as part of the Dubai Fitness Challenge.
Dedicated events will also mark Commemoration Day and Eid Al Etihad.Eng.
Mohammed Zaher Hammadih said, “As we mark our 15th season, Dubai Miracle Garden continues to bring people together through shared experiences.

Our weekly programme gives families a new reason to return, with cultural celebrations, live entertainment and activities to enjoy throughout the season.”The garden showcases more than 150 flower varieties alongside its signature floral structures, which have earned it multiple Guinness World Records.Since opening in 2013, Dubai Miracle Garden has welcomed millions of visitors and established itself as one of the region’s leading family attractions, contributing to Dubai’s appeal as a global tourism destination.Dubai Miracle Garden will welcome visitors daily from 8 October 2026 to 31st May 2027.
Opening hours are from 9am to 9pm on weekdays and from 9am to 11pm on weekends.
Entry is free for children under the age of three.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai Municipality launches ‘A Generation for a Greater Tomorrow’ initiative
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 8th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Dubai Municipality has launched the community initiative ‘A Generation for a Greater Tomorrow’, bringing children and their families together through an interactive experience that introduces them to the Municipality’s diverse areas of work and demonstrates how municipal services contribute to the way the city functions and supports everyday life. The initiative will take place at City Centre Mirdif from 7 to 11 October, from 10:00am to 10:00pm.The initiative combines education, exploration and recreation through a series of interactive stations designed to help children gain knowledge and develop skills through age-appropriate activities, games and practical experiences. The programme also provides opportunities for families to participate together, in line with the UAE’s Year of the Family and its emphasis on strengthening family participation and engagement.Through a range of experiences, children can explore different aspects of municipal work and gain a better understanding of their connection to everyday life. An agriculture-focused station introduces children to local plant species and the basics of growing seedlings, preparing soil, and applying effective irrigation and cultivation methods, highlighting the role of agriculture and green spaces in the city.The initiative also introduces children to basic health and safety practices at home and in public spaces. Activities cover common household tools and key safety principles relating to roads, beaches, parks and other public places, helping children connect what they learn with situations they may encounter in their daily lives.A dedicated platform focuses on communication, creativity and content creation, giving children an opportunity to develop their speaking and presentation skills, express their ideas and explore different ways of creating and sharing content.The programme also features interactive digital games that introduce children to municipal services in an accessible and age-appropriate way. One game explores health and safety management, including public health services related to veterinary care and pet welfare, while another introduces waste management and the importance of proper waste handling in maintaining the city’s cleanliness and sustainability.An interactive laboratory platform gives children an introduction to the world of laboratories through simple scientific experiments, while demonstrating the role of laboratories in municipal work and their relevance to everyday life.Through ‘A Generation for a Greater Tomorrow’, Dubai Municipality aims to strengthen children’s understanding of municipal work while giving them opportunities to explore their interests and develop skills across different fields and areas of specialisation. The initiative also provides an opportunity to engage with the aspirations of the next generation and strengthen their connection with the work that contributes to developing Dubai and enhancing the quality of life of its residents, supporting the continued development of a more attractive, sustainable and liveable city.

source_snapshot.title: Maktoum bin Mohammed reviews Dubai economic, financial indicators
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 8th October, 2026 (WAM) -- H.H. Sheikh Maktoum bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, First Deputy Ruler of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister, Minister of Finance and Chairman of the Higher Committee for the Development of the Economic and Financial Sector, chaired a meeting of the Committee to review the latest performance indicators across Dubai’s economic and financial sectors.The meeting highlighted the emirate’s progress across several global financial competitiveness indices and reviewed proposed strategic directions to reinforce Dubai’s standing as a leading, integrated global hub for gold.H.H. Sheikh Maktoum bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum emphasised that Dubai, guided by the vision and directives of His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President and Prime Minister of the UAE and Ruler of Dubai, continues to advance its economic competitiveness, develop its financial and economic sectors, build integrated ecosystems to drive sustainable growth, and further reinforce its position among the world’s leading hubs for business, finance and trade.H.H. stated: “Guided by the vision and directives of His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, we continue Dubai’s journey of economic diversification, competitiveness and sustainability. We continue to reinforce the emirate’s standing as a global hub for business, finance and trade by developing more competitive economic and financial sectors that are better capable of attracting investments, talent and global companies.”During the meeting, the Committee reviewed Dubai’s competitiveness indicators in the financial sector, which showed the emirate ranking first globally in FinTech on the Global Financial Centres Index (GFCI) published in September 2026, rising from fifth place in March 2026.Dubai also advanced to become second globally in Professional Services (up from fourth) and sixth in reputation (up from eighth), reflecting its continuous rise among top international financial centres.For the fourth consecutive time, Dubai maintained its leading position among global financial centres expected to become more significant over the next two to three years, in a testament to global confidence in its ability to sustain growth and strengthen its role in the global financial economy.In the virtual assets sector, the number of licensed Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs) under the Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (VARA) rose to 52, with assets under management reaching AED28 billion. Furthermore, trading volumes among licensed VASPs reached approximately AED7.43 trillion over the past 12 months, highlighting the sector's rapid growth and Dubai's evolving regulatory ecosystem.Financial market indicators highlighted sustained momentum across the Dubai Financial Market (DFM), with market capitalisation reaching AED993.1 billion by the end of the third quarter of 2026. DFM also saw a 24.5% surge in average daily trading values, while institutional trading accounted for 71% of total trading value.DFM attracted 55,462 new investors during the first nine months of 2026, with international investors representing 72.1% of new entrants to the market, reflecting a broadening investor base and the market's strong appeal to global capital.Dubai International Financial Centre (DIFC) continues to reinforce its role as a premier platform for businesses and financial services, hosting over 10,000 active registered companies. These include 592 wealth and asset management firms, alongside 1,933 FinTech and innovation firms, and the largest concentration of hedge funds in the region, underscoring the ongoing expansion of Dubai's financial ecosystem and the growing base of international institutions leveraging the emirate as a launchpad for their regional and global operations.Reinforcing Dubai’s position as a global hub for goldAmong the strategic priorities addressed during the meeting, the Committee reviewed statistics on the gold sector in Dubai and the UAE, as well as proposed directions to develop a comprehensive strategy that reinforces Dubai’s position as a leading global hub for gold. The proposed strategy spans all components of the value chain, from supply, refining and trading, to storage, financing, pricing, digital tokenisation and retail.Figures reviewed by the Committee showed that Dubai’s foreign gold trade reached approximately AED1 trillion in 2025, an increase of 60% year-on-year. The volume of physical gold traded in the UAE reached around 2,750 tonnes, placing the country second globally among physical gold trading hubs, with an estimated 13–15% of globally traded gold passing through Dubai annually.Dubai’s geographic location reinforces its role as a vital link connecting bullion supply sources in Africa and Central Asia with major demand markets in India, China and across the globe. The precious metals, gemstones and diamonds ecosystem at the Dubai Multi Commodities Centre (DMCC) comprises over 1,500 member companies, while the Dubai Gold District, launched in 2026, hosts more than 1,000 retail gold and jewellery traders.This ecosystem has witnessed the launch of the UAE Good Delivery Standard and the establishment of the UAE Bullion Market Committee in 2021, followed by the launch of the Dubai Gold District in 2026, marking continuous institutional and regulatory development.Six key directions under the Dubai Gold StrategyThe Committee reviewed six proposed strategic directions for the development of the Dubai Gold Strategy. The first focuses on developing an integrated global market for gold trading by expanding market depth and connecting producers, refineries and buyers across Africa, the Middle East and Asia.The second direction focuses on strengthening Dubai’s position as a global hub for gold financing by exploring opportunities in gold-related financing, clearing, collateralisation, hedging and institutional trading.The third aims to solidify Dubai’s status as a trusted and neutral centre for gold storage, by enhancing secure storage capabilities for institutional and sovereign assets. The fourth direction addresses boosting the competitiveness of gold traded through Dubai by advancing traceability, transparency standards and advanced practices.The fifth direction addresses supporting Dubai’s role in gold price discovery by examining financial instruments and platforms that leverage market depth and liquidity. The sixth direction focuses on reinforcing Dubai’s standing as a premier global destination for jewellery and end-user demand, driving retail trade and consumer demand while enhancing market appeal for traders and investors.The meeting also approved the establishment of a committee chaired by His Excellency Abdulla bin Damithan to drive the execution of the approved strategic direction for the Dubai Gold Strategy, further develop and refine its initiatives, and coordinate with relevant entities to establish a clear implementation roadmap.The committee’s responsibilities include identifying actionable initiatives and defining roles and partners, as well as proposing a governance model and execution timelines. This approach ensures a structured transition from strategic directions to informed, adoption-ready initiatives, while fostering public-private sector partnerships.

source_snapshot.title: DHA welcomes 11th cohort to 'Tibb wa Uloom' programme
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 8th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Dubai Health Authority (DHA) has welcomed 49 students to the 11th cohort of the Tibb wa Uloom (Medicine and Sciences), its study sponsorship programme for Emirati students.The programme targets high-achieving secondary school graduates and university students who wish to study health specialities.The students met Dr Alawi AlSheikh-Ali, Director-General of DHA, at a gathering during which the sponsorship contracts for the new cohort were signed.Since the programme launched in 2016, a total of 618 students have enrolled to date, including 297 graduates. This reflects DHA's continued efforts to support and develop Emirati talent in health specialities and to prepare them to contribute to the progress of Dubai's health sector.Women made up 84.8 per cent of all students enrolled in the programme, compared with 15.2 per cent men.Medicine accounted for about 60 per cent of enrolments, followed by nursing and then allied health specialities, which include radiology, pharmacy, physiotherapy, nutrition and other health fields. The specialities covered by the programme have evolved over the years in line with health priorities and the needs of the sector. New specialities, including public health, have been added on the basis of a clinical capacity study, to ensure that Emirati talent is prepared in priority health areas.Asma Al Sharif, CEO of the Health Regulatory Sector at DHA, said that investing in Emirati talent is a cornerstone of the sustainable development of the health sector. She noted that enabling Emirati students to build academic and professional pathways in health specialities helps supply the sector with qualified professionals who can meet its needs and future aspirations.She added, “The Tibb wa Uloom Programme is a long-term investment in Emirati talent. It begins by supporting students throughout their academic journey and extends to preparing them to contribute effectively to the health sector.”She noted that the arrival of the 11th cohort reflects the continuity of this investment and the programme's role in building a new generation of Emirati health professionals.Dr Khawla Al Hajaj, Director of the Medical Education and Research Department at DHA, said that the programme provides an integrated support system for Emirati students throughout their studies, combining academic sponsorship with training opportunities and practical development. This helps build their knowledge and skills and prepares them for the transition to professional life after they complete their studies.She added that the programme aims to attract and prepare Emirati students who wish to study health specialities, according to defined criteria, supporting the preparation of qualified Emirati professionals who can contribute effectively to the health sector.

source_snapshot.title: ISEA2026 Dubai connects global dialogue with artistic experiences across city
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 9th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Dubai Culture and Arts Authority (Dubai Culture) has unveiled highlights of the artistic and academic programmes for the 31st International Symposium on Electronic/Emerging Art (ISEA2026 Dubai), taking place from 6 to 15 November 2026 under the theme ‘ELYAH: Constellating Place, Data and Identity’. Exploring the intersection of art, science and technology, the symposium supports Dubai Culture’s Digital Arts Roadmap by expanding opportunities for creative talent, encouraging experimentation and advancing the digital and emerging arts sector. It also reinforces Dubai’s position as a global cultural reference, a leader in innovation and a driver of the creative economy, rooted in Emirati heritage.ISEA2026 Dubai will adopt a hybrid format, combining an in-person artistic programme across multiple venues in Dubai with an online academic programme. This approach will enable artists, researchers and practitioners worldwide to exchange ideas and expertise while connecting international dialogue with artistic experiences across the city. The artistic programme attracted more than 1,000 submissions, with over 100 artworks shortlisted, while more than 150 submissions were shortlisted for the academic programme. The agenda includes over 140 academic papers, more than 40 artist talks and sessions, over 15 workshops, more than 10 panel discussions, seven Eco Labs and four special-track exhibitions and sessions.The academic programme will feature keynote addresses, paper presentations, specialist panels and artist talks. A key strand, the New Media Art Summit, will explore how artistic practices are evolving through digital networks, immersive environments, interactive media and artificial intelligence, connecting research and curatorial perspectives with artistic production, and Eco Labs will examine the relationship between ecological systems, technology and artistic practice.Across Dubai, the artistic programme will bring audiences into contact with digital and emerging art through exhibitions, performances and immersive experiences. The programme includes exhibitions across 20 locations including Al Safa Art & Design Library, Etihad Museum, Kanvas and Foundry Gallery, experiences at ARTE Museum, performances at TODA, and projection mapping at Al Wasl Dome. It will also feature the special track Evolving Calligraphy, Letter Art, Typography, including Calligraphy to Code, exploring how letterforms, writing systems and calligraphic traditions are being reimagined through digital and computational media. These activities will give residents and visitors opportunities to engage with contemporary artistic practice and explore how technology is shaping new forms of expression.Maitha Ali Al Blooshi, Director of the Emerging Arts Department at Dubai Culture, highlighted the symposium’s role in strengthening Dubai’s international cultural presence and connecting creative practices and disciplines. She said: “The response to ISEA2026 Dubai from around the world reflects the emirate’s ability to bring together artists, researchers and practitioners within an environment that encourages innovation and the exchange of ideas. The symposium will give local talent opportunities to learn, experiment and build connections with specialised international networks.”She added: “ISEA2026 Dubai brings together diverse disciplines and expertise, creating opportunities for art, research and technology to inform one another. Through collaboration and the development of artistic practice, it supports the growth and sustainability of the digital and emerging arts sector. It also provides a platform to explore how technology, imagination, knowledge and culture can come together to generate new ideas, artworks and creative approaches.”The theme ‘ELYAH: Constellating Place, Data and Identity’ connects four core academic tracks. Celestial Dialogues explores art, technology and the cosmic imagination, examining how the sky and planetary systems shape human experience and cultural meaning. Charting Constellations focuses on mapping, networks, place and identity, exploring the connections between people, data, geographies and stories. Eco-Tech Futures examines ecology, climate, and technological responsibility through artistic practice, while Starlinked Worlds explores how artificial intelligence, digital networks, and virtual environments are changing the ways people create, connect, and share cultural experiences.

source_snapshot.title: MBRSC, UNOOSA announce call for proposals for third opportunity under Payload Hosting Initiative
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 9th October, 2026 (WAM) -- The Mohammed Bin Rashid Space Centre (MBRSC) and United Nations Office for Outer Space Affairs (UNOOSA) have announced the opening of applications for PHI-3, the third opportunity under the Payload Hosting Initiative (PHI), during the 77th International Astronautical Congress (IAC 2026) in Antalya, Türkiye.PHI is a joint programme by MBRSC in partnership with UNOOSA initiative ‘Access to Space for All’, which helps countries build practical space capabilities through hands-on opportunities. Through PHI, MBRSC develops and provides a 12U CubeSat platform to host innovative payloads and emerging space technologies from around the world. The programme offers partners the opportunity to test and validate their technologies in orbit, while participating in a real space mission supported by MBRSC’s technical and operational capabilities.Amer AlSayegh AlGhaferi, Assistant Director General of the Aerospace Engineering Sector, MBRSC, said, “PHI reflects our shared vision with UNOOSA to expand access to space and create meaningful opportunities for emerging space entities and nations to participate directly in real missions. Programmes such as PHI play an important role in broadening participation in the global space sector. By combining MBRSC’s satellite development and operational capabilities with UNOOSA’s international capacity-building framework, we are creating a pathway for new ideas, technologies and talent to reach space and generate knowledge that can support future missions and applications.”Aarti Holla-Maini, Director of UNOOSA, said, “Access to space is about much more than reaching orbit. It is about building the skills, experience and confidence that enable countries and institutions to develop their own space capabilities. PHI gives teams a practical first step on that journey. I strongly encourage teams from countries that have not yet had the opportunity to access space to apply for PHI-3.”The third mission builds on the first two PHI opportunities and continues the programme’s focus on providing an inclusive platform for testing, collaboration and innovation, enabling companies, universities, research centres and emerging space entities to contribute to the global space ecosystem. The programme also supports knowledge exchange across satellite design, manufacturing, testing, launch, operations and data analysis. The first satellite under the initiative, PHI-1 was launched in November 2025 with payloads from Bahrain Space Agency, Antarikchya Pratisthan Nepal, Sharjah Space and Astronomy Hub and the Centre. For PHI-2, the Technical University of Moldova (TUM) and Madari Space Limited of the UAE were selected to launch their payloads into space. Applications for PHI-3 will remain open until 6 April 2027. Following the submission period, proposals will be evaluated jointly by MBRSC and UNOOSA, with the selected awardees expected to be announced in the last quarter of 2027.

The results showed that Dubai’s cashless transactions index reached 90.1%, exceeding the 90% target set for 2026. The report showed that cashless payment initiatives contributed more than AED8 billion to the emirate’s economy. source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 9th October, 2026 (WAM) -- The Rental Disputes Centre (RDC) in Dubai concluded 2,350 rental disputes through amicable settlements worth a total of AED401 million in the first nine months of 2026, with an average resolution time of six days per case.The results highlight the effectiveness of the RDC's conciliation procedures in resolving rental disputes efficiently while protecting the legal rights of all parties.The figures also reflect the centre's efforts to improve dispute resolution mechanisms and judicial services amid continued growth in Dubai's rental market.Judge Abdulqader Mousa Mohammed, Chairman of the Rental Disputes Centre, said the results demonstrated the effectiveness of amicable settlements in resolving disputes swiftly while maintaining procedural standards and protecting the rights of those involved.He added that the RDC continues to develop its legal framework to support stable contractual relationships and strengthen confidence in Dubai's judicial system.Conciliation is a key alternative dispute resolution mechanism used by the RDC, allowing landlords and tenants to reach mutually agreed settlements without resorting to formal litigation.Settlement agreements are approved by a supervising judge, giving them the force of an enforceable legal instrument.The process also helps reduce the social and economic costs of prolonged disputes while promoting cooperation between the parties.The RDC said it remains committed to improving procedural efficiency, ensuring fair access to justice and promoting amicable settlements as an effective means of resolving rental disputes in Dubai.

source_snapshot.title: MBRHE marks World Habitat Day
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 10th October, 2026 (WAM) -- The Mohammed Bin Rashid Housing Establishment (MBRHE) is marking World Habitat Day with an interactive stand at Dubai Festival City Mall.The initiative showcases MBRHE’s services, initiatives and housing solutions while strengthening direct engagement with the community.MBRHE invites visitors to explore its range of services and latest housing solutions, speak directly with specialists and receive information to help them understand the available services and how to access them.The Establishment emphasised that the occasion highlights the importance of housing in supporting family stability and enhancing quality of life. It also reaffirms MBRHE’s commitment to developing an integrated housing system that meets citizens’ needs and future aspirations while providing a more convenient, efficient and sustainable housing experience.Dubai Islamic Bank is participating through a dedicated section within the stand, showcasing services and solutions offered in collaboration with MBRHE. Visitors can learn about the available options and receive answers to their related enquiries.The stand also features competitions, interactive activities, prize draws and instant prizes for visitors. These activities aim to encourage public participation and create an engaging community atmosphere that combines information about housing services with entertainment.The event forms part of MBRHE’s ongoing efforts to strengthen its community presence and expand customer engagement channels, raising awareness of its housing services and solutions and helping citizens benefit from them.

source_snapshot.title: WETEX 2026 to spotlight AI, workplace health, safety
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 10th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Dubai Electricity and Water Authority (DEWA) will organise the 28th edition of the Water, Energy, Technology and Environment Exhibition (WETEX) from 20th to 22nd October 2026 at the Dubai World Trade Centre, under the patronage of H.H. Sheikh Ahmed bin Saeed Al Maktoum, Chairman of the Dubai Supreme Council of Energy. The Health and Safety Hub at WETEX 2026 will host a range of activities and exhibitions, including the Health and Safety Conference, which will feature discussions on the latest developments in occupational health and safety in schools, homes and workplaces. The conference will bring together senior executives and experts from around the world in health, safety, wellbeing, emergency preparedness and emerging workplace risks. Discussions will focus on promoting health and wellbeing, using artificial intelligence and emerging technologies to manage risks, and improving quality of life through effective governance.Saeed Mohammed Al Tayer, MD and CEO of DEWA and Founder and Chairman of WETEX, said the exhibition supports the Dubai Social Agenda 33 and the National Strategy for Wellbeing 2031, which aims to position the UAE as a global leader in quality of life.He said the conference will highlight innovations and technologies that strengthen health and safety practices, protect people and safeguard property and the environment.The Health and Safety Conference’s panel discussions include ‘Discover the Future of HSE: Build Your Own AI + Vibe Coding Solution for Breakthrough Health & Safety Performance’, ‘Building Trust in AI Systems: Transparency, Ethics and Compliance and What They Mean in Practice’, ‘AI Fusion: Trust, Behaviour and Psychological Safety in the AI-Augmented Workplace’, ‘From Data to Prevention: Using AI and Analytics to Support Health, Safety and Environmental Decision Making’, ‘Workforce Wellbeing and Behavioural Safety in a Digital Era’, ‘AI and Robotics as Safety Enablers: Lessons from the Industrial Frontline’ and ‘Data-Driven Leadership: Turning Safety Data into Actionable Insights’.

source_snapshot.title: The Ripe Market opens in Dubai: Here’s what to eat, shop, and do this season
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: The aroma of freshly brewed coffee and baked cookies, the buzz of shoppers browsing independent brands, and the sound of children’s giggles and live entertainment set the scene as The Ripe Market returned to Dubai Police Academy Park in Umm Suqeim today, marking 15 years of bringing local businesses and communities together.The opening of the new season on October 10 has welcomed visitors back to one of Dubai’s familiar weekend destinations, where shopping, food, and family activities come together in an outdoor setting. With stalls to explore, food to enjoy, and activities for all ages, the market offers residents an opportunity to slow down and spend a few hours enjoying the bazaar..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..A treasure hunt for homegrown brandsFor shoppers, a walk through The Ripe Market offers the chance to discover products beyond the usual retail shelves. Independent businesses showcase everything from fashion, jewellery, and accessories to homeware, artwork, beauty products, and handcrafted gifts.Among the returning participants is Hasabi Organic Farm Al Ain, which brings locally grown organic vegetables to the market..“These are all local and organic vegetables from our farm. Every day, they are freshly harvested,” Riyad Hossin, a salesman at the farm, told Gulf News.“We have been participating for 12 years now, and it really helps because customers are coming.”.Further along, shoppers can discover Birs Atelier, where handbags are handmade using recycled materials, with customised designs and individual stitching.“We create handmade handbags with customised designs. We use recycled materials, and we do everything ourselves, every stitch by hand,” shared owner Birsan Kan.“We have different sizes and price points. You can find a piece of your childhood in every design, and everything is locally made here in the UAE.”.Kan has noted that her participation in the market has helped her business grow, prompting her to take a more permanent presence this season.“This is my second year participating in The Ripe Market, and this time I have decided to have a permanent place because it helps my business grow. The Ripe Market has a lot of footfall and marketing around brands, and I want to be part of it.”.Upcycled wood turns into a speakerFor those interested in sustainable products, Mango Beat demonstrates an unusual take on the smartphone speaker, giving discarded material a new purpose.“The idea is to create a speaker and amplifier for smartphones without using wires, batteries, or electricity. It is one piece of wood, and it is upcycled,” explained Charles Jabbour, a partner at Mango Beat.“We buy used wood and upcycle it into something completely handmade.”.Jabbour has bared that the larger speakers can amplify sound by up to seven times, while the smaller ones can amplify it by up to five times.The business also works with farming communities in Thailand to repurpose waste wood and turn it into products for international markets.Jabbour has participated at the Academy Park location for about eight years and highlighted that the market offers a valuable opportunity to connect with people interested in sustainability.“It is a great place to connect with the community. You have a lot of people here who are professionals and work in ESG (environmental, social, and governance) and sustainability.” He added, “It is great to introduce our product, which resonates with a lot of people and is not something you find in many places.”.Follow the sweet treatsShopping is only part of the experience. The market also brings together food concepts serving breakfast, coffee, street food, sweet treats, and family-friendly favourites.Visitors can begin their morning with a coffee and breakfast, stop for a meal between shopping trips, or pick up something sweet while exploring the stalls.The variety of food and drink options makes it easy to turn a short visit into a longer outing, whether meeting friends, supporting a local food business, or taking a break from the activities..For Tatiano Kamoeva, a marketing director who visited the market, the appeal extends beyond shopping.“Padel brought me here, but I also love crafted things and everything that is handmade. I love the handmade plates, some drinks and food,” exclaimed Kamoev.“You can get a lot of entertainment and cultural things. It is a great place.”.Visitor Elle McCabe, an operations manager, has mentioned that she came to support a friend who has a fine-dining booth at the market.“My friend has a fine-dining booth, and I came to see and support them. This place is absolutely fab. The baby shops are also really cute,” described McCab..Keeping children busyFor families, The Ripe Market offers more than shopping and food. Children can look forward to activities including a petting zoo, pony rides, arts and crafts, workshops, inflatables, mini train rides, and a carousel.The range of attractions gives younger visitors plenty to explore, whether they want to spend time with animals, get creative at a workshop, or enjoy the rides. Parents can browse the stalls or stop for a meal while making time for activities that appeal to the whole family.The market's stage will also host family-friendly entertainment throughout the season, including magic shows, music, and themed performances..For Emma Pilal, who attended the opening with her son Danis, the magic show was a highlight of their visit.“I came here for the magic show, and we really enjoyed it. We will definitely come back to explore the other shops and activities,” remarked Pilal.The market's open-air setting allows families to move between the attractions, shopping stalls, and food outlets, making it possible to enjoy several experiences during one visit..Dubai Police bring community activities to the marketDubai Police will once again take part in the market's community programme, with activities planned throughout the season.Visitors can look forward to performances by the Dubai Police Marching Band, K9 demonstrations, and displays of Dubai Police supercars. Children will also have opportunities to participate in activities, alongside appearances by officer Amna and captain Mansour.The programme adds another attraction for families and gives younger visitors opportunities to engage with Dubai Police in a community setting..Live performances add to the weekend atmosphereBeyond the shopping stalls and food counters, live entertainment will feature throughout the season, with music, themed musical acts, magic shows, and family-friendly performances planned.Homegrown performers will be part of the programme, offering visitors a chance to pause between activities, gather around the stage, and enjoy live acts in an informal outdoor setting.The entertainment schedule will change throughout the season, giving regular visitors different performances and activities to discover on return visits..Make room for wellness and sportThose looking to do more than shop and eat can also explore the market's wellness and sports offering.Free sessions will include yoga, Pilates, sound healing, and mindfulness, giving visitors opportunities to stretch, unwind, or take a break from the pace of everyday life.Sports activities planned throughout the season will include swimming, padel, tennis, horse riding, football, rugby, and gymnastics.The mix of activities is designed to appeal to different ages and interests, making the market an option for visitors who want to combine a social outing with an active weekend..15 years of bringing communities togetherAs The Ripe Market enters its 15th year, its story goes beyond the products on its stalls. It is also about the small businesses that have found customers, the makers who have shared their craft, and the families and friends who have returned to spend their weekends together.For vendors such as Al Ain Hasabi Organic Farm and Mango Beat, years of participation have helped build connections with customers and the wider community. For businesses such as Birs Atelier, the market offers a platform to grow, while visitors come for everything from handmade finds and food to entertainment and time with family..In a city as diverse as Dubai, The Ripe Market brings these different experiences together in one place, creating opportunities for people to discover local talent, support independent businesses, and connect with others.As another season begins, the market’s 15-year milestone is a reminder that its lasting appeal lies not just in what visitors take home, but in the people they meet and the community they become part of.The Ripe Market runs every Saturday and Sunday from 9am to 9pm at Dubai Police Academy Park in Umm Suqeim until May 2 next year..The Ripe Market is back: What to expect at Dubai Police Academy Park this season.Inside Abu Dhabi Mall’s Ripe Market, where local creativity takes centre stage.What the Khorfakkan Mango Festival offers to local farmers and families.Hatta Farming Festival 2026: 7 rare finds you can buy from Emirati farmers at the local market

source_snapshot.title: Dubai Police recognised at global summit in Seoul for project management excellence
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 10th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Dubai Police has received international recognition from the Project Management Institute (PMI) for its excellence in planning, managing and delivering projects and initiatives in line with global professional standards.The recognition was announced during the PMI Global Summit Series Seoul, the Republic of Korea, which brought together project management leaders, experts and specialists from around the world.The achievement recognises the work of the Initiatives and Projects Department within Dubai Police’s General Department of Excellence and Pioneering and highlights the force’s approach to turning strategic plans into practical projects with measurable results.Dubai Police has developed an integrated project management system built around effective planning, good governance and measuring performance and impact. The system helps ensure that initiatives are delivered efficiently, resources are managed effectively, and projects contribute to the force’s wider strategic objectives.Major General Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah Rashid Al Mualla, Director of the General Department of Excellence and Pioneering at Dubai Police, said the recognition reflects Dubai Police’s forward-looking approach to project management, enabling the organisation to translate strategic priorities into actionable plans and meaningful, sustainable outcomes.“This recognition from the Project Management Institute, one of the world’s leading professional organisations in the field, reflects the maturity of Dubai Police’s institutional practices and the capabilities of its personnel in managing projects through governance, flexibility, impact measurement and future foresight,” he said.

source_snapshot.title: Hamdan bin Mohammed names RTA winner of Dubai-it Award for Institutions in the Field of Government
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 11th October, 2026 (WAM) -- H.H. Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence, and Chairman of The Executive Council of Dubai, congratulated the Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) in Dubai on winning the ‘Dubai-it Award’ for Institutions in the Field of Government.The award recognises RTA’s tangible results in accelerating services, improving operational efficiency, and enhancing customer experience across the roads and transport sectors, as well as its adoption of the ‘Dubai-it’ philosophy as an institutional culture and work approach.H.H. Sheikh Hamdan stated, “We announced the Dubai-it Award to celebrate Dubai’s philosophy of work, brought to life by His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President and Prime Minister of the UAE and Ruler of Dubai. Dubai-it means achieving something extraordinary with excellence in record time.”Sheikh Hamdan added, “Today, RTA receives the award for Institutions in the Field of Government. It delivers major roads, bridges and tunnels at 2x global benchmarks for speed and efficiency without compromising quality. Metro punctuality stands at 99.7 percent as the network continues to expand with more stations. Autonomous mobility and high-quality cycling routes advance at pace. Anticipating the city’s needs. Enabling Dubai’s next phase of growth. This is how RTA does Dubai-it. Congratulations to the team.”The Roads and Transport Authority won the award for adopting the ‘Dubai-it’ philosophy as an institutional culture and work approach based on delivering exceptional projects in record time and achieving tangible, high-quality results that reinforce Dubai's status as a global benchmark in mobility, infrastructure, and government services.The Authority embodied the Dubai-it philosophy by executing major road, bridge, and tunnel projects at double the global speed and efficiency rates, including iconic projects such as the Infinity Bridge. It maintained the highest average pace of delivery across bridges, tunnels and infrastructure projects, equivalent to double the global completion speed, at a cost below the global average, while ensuring superior quality.The Authority achieved a Dubai Metro punctuality rate of 99.7 percent, alongside the continuous expansion of the metro network and station upgrades. It developed systems to monitor and address road feedback in under 24 hours and accelerated dozens of driver and vehicle-related services, making them among the fastest globally.Furthermore, RTA executed a series of road projects and over 250 traffic improvements that contributed to cutting travel times by up to 60 percent. It developed and operated AI-powered autonomous taxis to support the future of mobility in Dubai, developed the Air Taxi Station in Dubai to add a new mode to the city's future mobility ecosystem, and expanded and improved cycle tracks with high quality and in record time.Additionally, RTA implemented 117 quick-win improvements within two years and succeeded in providing 82 services without any waiting time, reflecting its focus on reducing completion times and responding faster to the needs of transport network users.These accomplishments reflect Dubai’s philosophy of work, ‘Dubai-it’: achieving something extraordinary with excellence in record time.Mohammad Abdullah Al Gergawi, Chairman of the Executive Office of Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, said, “The Dubai-it Award received hundreds of nominations reflecting great diversity in initiatives, projects, and achievements that embody Dubai’s work philosophy. They demonstrate the ability of individuals and institutions to turn ambitions into tangible results. RTA's approach clearly reflected this philosophy on the ground by combining quality, speed, and continuity, turning challenges into opportunities for development and service improvement.”He said, “RTA’s recognition with the Dubai-it Award for Institutions in the Field of Government highlights an institutional model built on sustained achievement, rapid responsiveness, precision in execution, and tangible impact on society. It embodies Dubai-it: achieving something extraordinary with excellence in record time, creating lasting impact that strengthens Dubai’s competitiveness and quality of life.”Al Gergawi added, “The award sheds light on the Authority's efforts in converting feedback into measurable improvements, its commitment to innovation to simplify procedures and advance services, and its implementation of continuous improvements to boost efficiency and elevate the customer experience in Dubai.”His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President, Prime Minister and Ruler of Dubai, launched the Dubai-it initiative to advance the philosophy of work behind Dubai’s transformation: bold ambition, excellent execution, and the determination to make the extraordinary happen.The initiative aims to embed this philosophy across institutions and companies, making it a shared culture and an enduring way of working. To see beyond what exists. To act with speed and the highest standards. To create lasting value for the city and its people, with every achievement opening the way for the next.Under the directives of H.H. Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, the Dubai-it Award was launched to honour the individuals, projects, companies, and institutions that bring this philosophy to life. An annual recognition of bold ambition, excellence in execution, and lasting impact. By celebrating those who turn possibility into achievement, the award sets the pace for Dubai’s future development goals.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai doubles Oraseya Capital fund to AED1 billion to accelerate AI, fintech and future-tech investment
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: The Dubai Integrated Economic Zones Authority (DIEZ) has doubled the size of the venture capital fund managed by its investment arm, Oraseya Capital, from AED500 million to AED1 billion, strengthening its capacity to support high-potential companies and reinforcing Dubai's position as a global hub for venture capital, innovation and future industries. The expansion is designed to increase support for technology companies with global growth potential while advancing the objectives of the Dubai Economic Agenda D33. His Highness Sheikh Ahmed bin Saeed Al Maktoum, Chairman of DIEZ, said: "Doubling the size of the Oraseya Capital fund reflects our confidence in Dubai's position as a hub for technology leaders and translates the directives of His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President and Prime Minister of the UAE and Ruler of Dubai, to build a diversified, knowledge-based economy driven by innovation." He added: "Expanding the fund's capacity strengthens the ecosystem around promising companies, providing them with the capital, expertise and opportunities they need to grow from Dubai into regional and global markets." "We have strong confidence in Dubai's future as a global centre for capital and innovation. Our role is to translate this confidence into tangible investments, companies and economic opportunities that contribute to the objectives of the Dubai Economic Agenda D33, strengthen Dubai's competitiveness, and reinforce the UAE's position as a global hub for the new economy and investment in future-focused sectors," Sheikh Ahmed said. DIEZ has also increased Oraseya Capital's maximum investment per company from USD3 million to USD6 million, equivalent to approximately AED22 million, enabling the fund to participate in larger funding rounds and support companies at more advanced stages of growth. The fund's investment scope will expand beyond companies directly linked to the UAE to include global businesses of strategic relevance to the country, opening access to a wider range of opportunities across international markets. Under the expanded mandate, Oraseya Capital will support founders at every stage of growth, including companies beyond Series B funding rounds. The move will allow the fund to back businesses with proven models and demonstrated growth potential while continuing to support early-stage start-ups. DIEZ said the strategy is aimed at helping build the next generation of billion-dollar unicorn companies, strengthening Dubai's position as a global business hub and a launchpad for regional and international expansion. Strong track record Oraseya Capital has established itself as one of the region's most active venture capital investors since its launch. According to venture capital data platform MAGNiTT, the fund has ranked as the UAE's most active investor by number of deals for three consecutive years. It ranked first in the UAE in 2024 and retained the position in 2025. In MAGNiTT's first-half 2026 rankings, it remained the UAE's most active investor by both overall deal count and early-stage investment activity, while placing second across the Middle East and North Africa in both categories. The fund was also named Venture Capital Firm of the Year at the Entrepreneur Middle East Awards 2025. His Excellency Dr Mohammed Al Zarooni, Executive Chairman of DIEZ. His Excellency Dr Mohammed Al Zarooni, Executive Chairman of DIEZ, said: "Doubling the size of the fund reflects the strength of Oraseya Capital's model and the results it has achieved since its launch. "It enhances our capacity to respond to the ambitions and needs of promising companies at different stages of growth, while creating opportunities for more impactful investment partnerships. "We are taking Oraseya Capital into a new phase of growth and expansion guided by a clear investment approach that brings together capital, expertise, guidance and access to an integrated network of investors and partners," he added. Dr Al Zarooni said DIEZ's ambition extends beyond investing in start-ups to supporting companies capable of competing on the global stage, with Dubai serving as their base for expansion. Portfolio companies raise USD1.1 billion Since its launch in November 2023, Oraseya Capital has built a portfolio of 66 active companies and has averaged 25 investments annually. The fund has completed eight cohorts of its SANDBOX programme, which provides selected companies with USD150,000 in funding, alongside its six-month LAUNCHPAD programme for entrepreneurs. Portfolio companies have increased their combined annual recurring revenue from approximately USD180 million at the time of investment to USD387 million today, including USD140 million generated within the UAE. The companies have also raised a combined USD1.1 billion, underscoring their ability to attract follow-on funding and scale internationally. Oraseya Capital's portfolio spans sectors including fintech, proptech, artificial intelligence, medi

source_snapshot.title: MBRHE becomes first Dubai government entity to launch dedicated service area for ‘Generation Shapers’
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: The Mohammed Bin Rashid Housing Establishment (MBRHE) has announced the launch of a dedicated service area for "Generation Shapers", becoming the first government entity in Dubai to introduce the initiative. The move is aimed at enhancing customer experience and recognising the role of mothers in raising future generations and strengthening families and society. The dedicated area has been designed to provide a comfortable and convenient service experience by addressing the needs of customers classified as "Generation Shapers" and facilitating their access to MBRHE services. MBRHE said the initiative translates its appreciation of "Generation Shapers" into a practical institutional initiative, recognising their contribution to raising children, instilling values and supporting the development of a cohesive society. The initiative also aligns with the objectives of the UAE's Year of the Family 2026, which seeks to strengthen family bonds and reinforce the family as the foundation of society and a driver of development. MBRHE said it remains committed to developing people-centred government services that combine quality with responsiveness to the needs of different segments of society, supporting its vision of providing an integrated housing system that enhances quality of life and promotes family and social stability in Dubai. The initiative builds on MBRHE's broader efforts in institutional excellence. In March 2026, the establishment obtained international accreditation under the International Employee Happiness and Wellbeing Standard (IEHWS) and the International Digital Customer Experience Standard (IDCXS), achieving an evaluation score of 100 per cent in both standards. MBRHE said the accreditation reflects its commitment to applying international standards to improve the work environment, enhance customer experience and support continuous improvement in the delivery of housing services.

source_snapshot.title: 11 Dubai-based companies pledge to integrate Agentic AI into their operations
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 12th October, 2026 (WAM) -- In the presence of H.H. Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, a total of 11 Dubai-based companies representing diverse sectors have pledged to integrate Agentic AI technologies into their operations, with the support of Dubai Chambers.The pledge reflects the private sector's commitment to advancing the adoption of Agentic AI under Dubai's private sector Agentic AI transformation programme, launched in May this year by H.H. Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence of the UAE, and Chairman of the Executive Council of Dubai. Overseen by Dubai Chambers, the programme aims to enable businesses to harness the potential of these advanced technologies.The 11 companies that signed the pledge launched by Dubai Chambers are Emirates, DP World, AW Rostamani Group, Al Ansari Exchange, Dubai Islamic Bank, Kitopi, Dutco Group, Aster DM Healthcare, Innovo, Independent Food Company and HSA Group.Mohammad Ali Rashed Lootah, President and CEO of Dubai Chambers, said: “Agentic AI represents a new phase in the evolution of business models, offering significant opportunities for companies to transform their operations, improve service quality and make faster, more informed decisions. These capabilities can drive greater operational efficiency, productivity and innovation. Agentic AI also provides businesses with a strategic tool to support growth, adapt to rapid changes in the global business environment, turn challenges into opportunities for expansion and create sustainable value.”He added: “The pledge reflects growing recognition among businesses that Agentic AI is no longer a technology of the future, but an essential driver of efficiency, innovation and competitiveness. Its adoption will also enable companies to develop more agile operating models that can respond effectively to evolving business needs.”The pledge marks a practical step towards enabling companies to move beyond exploring the potential of Agentic AI to adopting intelligent solutions across their operations, including service development, internal processes and decision-making. The aim is to enhance productivity and operational efficiency while encouraging investment in technologies that support long-term growth and enable businesses to respond to rapidly changing market conditions.The participation of companies from diverse sectors reflects growing interest in adopting advanced technologies and reinforces collaboration between Dubai Chambers and the private sector to accelerate digital transformation. The initiative also contributes to developing a more innovative business environment that harnesses technology to create new economic opportunities and strengthen Dubai's global competitiveness.Dubai's private sector Agentic AI transformation programme, includes specialised training tracks recently launched by Dubai Chambers to support the adoption of these technologies. The training aims to equip more than 14,000 companies represented within Dubai Chamber of Commerce's Business Groups and Business Councils with the knowledge and capabilities needed to integrate Agentic AI into their administrative and operational activities.The programme also includes the establishment of specialised incubators for Agentic AI companies, alongside initiatives to support the development and adoption of Agentic AI solutions. Other areas of focus include developing young talent, expanding access to funding, facilitating knowledge sharing and strengthening capabilities across Dubai’s business community.

source_snapshot.title: AquaIndex plans to launch UAE water token as part of global expansion
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 12th October, 2026 (WAM) -- AquaIndex, a water asset management and pricing company, has announced plans to launch a dedicated regional water token for the UAE as part of its strategy to expand globally and build a digital infrastructure for the documentation, pricing, ownership management and trading of water reserves using real-world asset (RWA) tokenisation technology.Ahmed Bin Sulayem, Executive Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, DMCC, said, "When we signed our partnership with AquaIndex in 2025, our ambition was clear: to support the launch of what we believe is the world's first digital asset token backed directly by freshwater resources, to help develop a more transparent global marketplace for water, and to establish Dubai as a leading centre for this emerging sector." He added that Dubai remains a natural platform for the company's next phase of international growth. Through DMCC's ecosystem connecting trade, logistics, technology and finance, the partnership aims to bring physical assets into blockchain-powered markets and support better stewardship of water resources.AquaIndex expects its enterprise platform to go live in Q4 2026. The platform is designed to create standardised digital representations of certified physical water reserves, enabling the underlying assets to be documented, tracked and managed. It also incorporates an automated physical redemption and logistics engine, connecting smart-contract execution with physical delivery at certified reservoir and distribution locations. This is designed to enable holders of water tokens to redeem their allocation for physical water through established delivery infrastructure.The company's initial physical tokens are backed by water sourced from a regulated aquifer in the USA. The initial asset base proposed for tokenisation comprises up to 11 billion barrels of water, with an estimated value of approximately US$5 billion. The associated delivery network includes more than 20 miles of existing pipeline infrastructure, with individual pipelines offering potential physical delivery capacity of approximately 300,000 barrels per day at large scale.Yaacov Shirazi, Chairman and Founder of AquaIndex, said the company is building the technology layer that can connect the physical resource with transparent pricing, verified ownership and efficient delivery. He emphasised that the UAE, with its global commodities ecosystem and increasingly sophisticated digital infrastructure, is an important part of the company's global expansion strategy. Shirazi added, "We are not simply digitising an asset. We are building the infrastructure that connects the digital representation of water to the physical resource itself from verification and documentation through to redemption and delivery."AquaIndex is also developing its infrastructure on the Canton Network, including the operation of a dedicated Canton Network Validator Node to support data privacy and secure transactions. The company is simultaneously deploying its core smart-contract infrastructure on Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) architecture, supporting interoperability with wider digital technologies and automated logistics systems. It expects initial commodity allocations and secondary-market integrations to go live by the end of 2026, with further international reserve assets and commercial applications planned as the platform expands, alongside exploring growth opportunities across the GCC to support water security.

source_snapshot.title: 1 Billion Followers Summit opens submissions for $1 million AI Film Award 2027
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 12th October, 2026 (WAM) -- The 1 Billion Followers Summit has opened submissions for the second edition of the AI Film Award 2027, offering a $1 million grand prize to creators worldwide for AI-generated films exploring humanitarian, social and environmental issues.Organised in partnership with BytePlus, ByteDance's enterprise technology services arm, and supported this year by TikTok, the award aims to encourage innovative storytelling and expand the use of artificial intelligence in content creation.The winning film will be announced during the fifth edition of the 1 Billion Followers Summit, taking place in Dubai from 8th to 10th January 2027.Alia Al Hammadi, Vice Chairperson of the UAE Government Media Office and Deputy CEO of the 1 Billion Followers Summit, said the initiative supports the UAE's ambition to strengthen its position as a global hub for innovation, technology and the digital economy.She said, "The 1 Billion Followers Summit helps translate this vision into practical opportunities by bringing together creators, talent, technology companies, digital platforms and experts, providing a space to experiment with new ideas and transform them into stories and projects that reach the world."She added, "Through this award, we aspire to discover new talent capable of shaping the future of content creation and presenting inspiring examples that demonstrate how artificial intelligence can enhance human imagination rather than replace it."Al Hammadi said the award encourages creators to use AI responsibly and innovatively to explore new forms of expression, address societal issues and produce meaningful stories for global audiences.Long Li, General Manager for the Middle East and Africa at BytePlus, said the partnership reflects the importance of supporting creators and strengthening their connections with digital platforms and technology companies.He said, "The 1 Billion Followers Summit provides an important global platform for discovering talent and new ideas. The award combines human creativity with advanced AI capabilities, giving creators opportunities to explore new approaches to storytelling and address issues that matter to communities worldwide. We look forward to seeing the entries and the new perspectives they offer on the future of content creation in the age of AI."He added, "At BytePlus, we believe technology has the greatest impact when it gives creators more room to experiment and express themselves, helps them reach new audiences in innovative ways, and transforms their ideas into stories and visual experiences that reach a global audience."Entries will be assessed on AI integration, storytelling, creativity, aesthetics and technical execution.The competition covers five themes: Society, Community & Humanitarian Issues; Truth, Fake News & Misinformation; Humans & AI; Climate, Nature & Our Changing Planet; and Human Relationships.Applicants must be at least 18 years old and submit original films lasting five to seven minutes, in a cinematic 16:9 horizontal format, at 1080p resolution, as MOV or MP4 files. Films may be produced in any language but must include English subtitles. Creators retain ownership and copyright of their work.At least 70 percent of each finished film must be generated using ByteDance's Dreamina Seedance AI video-generation technology. Other AI tools, conventional editing techniques and original live-action footage may be used for supporting elements, provided the minimum Seedance requirement is met.Submissions will remain open until 20th November 2026, with the top 10 shortlisted films announced and public voting opening on 15th December, followed by the unveiling of the five finalists on 25th December. The finalists will be screened in Dubai, and the winner of the $1 million grand prize will be announced during the fifth edition of the 1 Billion Followers Summit, taking place from 8th to 10th January 2027.

source_snapshot.title: Will your Dubai school hike fees next year? How KHDA's 24-hour inspections and ratings come into play
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Dubai parents were relieved when school fees were frozen for the 2026-27 academic year. With the Knowledge and Human Development Authority (KHDA) bringing back school inspections, the big question now is whether your child's school will be allowed to raise fees next year since a school's inspection rating can influence its eligibility for an increase, if one is approved.Gulf News explains KHDA’s new model of inspection visits, when inspections will start, how ratings could affect eligibility, how appeals work and what will drive the final decision.Why is KHDA changing its inspections?According to KHDA, inspections are returning after a two-year pause. KHDA Director-General Aisha Miran said teachers and schools had asked for fewer inspections, so they had time to make improvements.Hence, after 17 years of annual inspections, she pushed for a pause, and KHDA now wants to see whether schools used that time well.What are QA 1 and QA 2?They are the new types of inspection visits named Quality Assurance 1 and Quality Assurance 2 visits.According to KHDA, QA 1 is a full, conventional inspection of the entire school against the 2015 UAE School Inspection Framework. A school’s overall rating could improve, decline or remain unchanged following the inspection.If a fee increase is approved, the school’s eligibility for an increase will be determined by its updated inspection rating.QA 2 is a targeted visit for schools where data indicates specific areas for improvement, but where a full inspection is not expected to change the school’s overall rating. KHDA will focus on those areas, offering advice and support to help schools improve.A QA 2 visit will not change a school’s existing rating. Therefore, if a fee increase is approved, schools undergoing QA 2 will have their eligibility for any increase assessed based on their existing inspection ratings from two years ago, in accordance with the applicable fee framework.Which schools will surely undergo QA1?Schools entering their third year of operation will undergo a comprehensive quality assurance visit covering overall performance, teaching standards, and learning outcomes.The assessment will conclude with a detailed report and an overall school rating.Why not inspect every school fully?According to KHDA, it wants to use its time and resources where they can make a difference. It will use school data, including learning outcomes, parental complaints and leadership evaluation, to decide who gets which visit.KHDA says artificial intelligence will support this, with human oversight. KHDA does not want to reassess schools that are already performing well.What are the new focus areas in inspections?KHDA will place additional emphasis on four areas: early childhood education, the quality of education for Emirati students, inclusive education for students of determination, and Arabic language teaching and learning.These priorities complement the existing UAE School Inspection Framework.Why only 24 hours' notice?Schools will get no more than 24 hours' notice. According to KHDA, the aim is for schools to maintain standards all year rather than preparing for a known inspection date. Miran said parents have told KHDA that schools can look very different when inspectors are expected. KHDA wants inspectors to see everyday teaching and interactions, and to have more confidence in the results.Will schools know which category they are in?Not in advance. According to KHDA, schools will find out whether they have QA 1 or QA 2 only 24 hours before the visit.Miran said KHDA has some initial indications, but the final decision will use the latest data.There is one exception. According to KHDA, any school entering its third year of operation will undergo a QA 1 inspection, as it is still considered new. Meanwhile, schools in their first or second year will get specialised visits instead.How could QA 1/QA 2 affect a fee increase?According to KHDA, fee increases are linked to a school's most recent inspection result. Some schools will have a rating from this academic year, while others will keep one from up to two years ago.A QA 2 school keeps its existing rating. For example, a school rated Very Good stays Very Good.For a QA 1 school, the new rating, whether higher, lower or unchanged, is what counts. source_snapshot.title: Resolve Dubai rental disputes quickly: Amicable solutions without court
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Landlords and tenants in Dubai are increasingly resolving rental disputes without lengthy court proceedings, with 2,350 cases worth Dh401 million settled amicably in an average of just six days during the first nine months of 2026.The figures, released by Dubai’s Rental Disputes Centre (RDC), highlight the growing importance of conciliation as a faster and less confrontational way to settle disagreements between property owners and tenants.Between January and September 2026, the centre successfully concluded 2,350 amicable settlement cases, helping disputing parties reach mutually acceptable solutions while protecting their legal rights.How the settlement process workUnder the RDC’s conciliation system, landlords and tenants involved in rental disagreements are given an opportunity to resolve their differences through a structured legal process.Rather than proceeding directly to formal litigation, both parties can negotiate a mutually acceptable agreement with the assistance of the centre’s Conciliation and Settlement Department.Once an agreement is reached, it is approved by a supervising judge, giving it the legal force of an enforceable instrument.This means the settlement is not merely an informal understanding but a legally enforceable agreement designed to protect the rights of both parties.Greater confidenceJudge Abdulqader Mousa Mohammed, Chairman of the Rental Disputes Centre, said the results demonstrated the effectiveness of Dubai’s approach to resolving rental disagreements.“The performance of the amicable settlement mechanism during the first nine months of this year underscores its capacity to bring rental disputes to swift and effective conclusions and confirms that timely resolution, procedural quality, and the protection of rights are all integral outcomes of efforts grounded in specialised expertise and an immediate response to the needs of disputing parties. The RDC continues to advance its legal framework to support the stability of contractual relationships and foster confidence in Dubai’s judicial system.”Why amicable settlements matterFor landlords and tenants, amicable settlements offer an opportunity to resolve disputes without the time and uncertainty often associated with formal court proceedings.The process allows both sides to negotiate practical solutions while preserving contractual relationships wherever possible.According to the RDC, the approach also helps reduce the social and economic consequences of prolonged rental disagreements.As Dubai’s rental market continues to grow, the centre said it remains focused on improving dispute resolution procedures, ensuring fair access to justice and encouraging landlords and tenants to settle disagreements through conciliation. .Dubai rental dispute process: How to file a case, fees, documents and what happens next.Ajman issues new decree setting fees and deposits for rental dispute cases.Dubai landlord refusing to return your security deposit?
