The architecture spans digital low-voltage switchboards, a building management system, EcoStruxure Power Operation at VDX integrated with the Dubai Marina Vertiport, ION9000 power quality monitoring, connected power meters, capacitor banks, and Galaxy UPS protecting critical systems.Every element serves one of three outcomes:Operational resilience keeps the vertiport flight-ready, with real-time visibility into the health of critical power and building systems so potential issues are addressed before they reach operations.Energy intelligence optimises consumption across the facility and enables aircraft charging that adapts dynamically to demand.Network scalability turns the vertiport into a blueprint: a standardised digital architecture that shares infrastructure status automatically with flight scheduling and charging systems, and can be replicated at every station that follows.Once the site is fully operational, Schneider Electric's solutions are expected to deliver energy savings of up to 25% across the facility.The project supports the Dubai 2040 Urban Master Plan and its 20-Minute City policy, which envisions a city where residents reach most of their daily destinations within 20 minutes.

Journeys that take 45 minutes by road are expected to take approximately 12 minutes by air, placing Dubai among the first cities in the world to make electric air travel part of everyday urban mobility.“Charging electric aircraft creates some pretty significant and rapidly changing power demands,” said Gareth Wilson, General Manager, Dubai, Skyports Infrastructure.

“At the same time, the terminal and all of its critical systems need to stay fully operational.We chose Schneider Electric to provide us with power infrastructure that is resilient, responsive and intelligent.
Most importantly, the scalable approach gives us something we can replicate across the wider Dubai network.

As we continue to add more vertiports, it provides us with a baseline that we can confidently continue to roll out.”"Our collaboration with Skyports Infrastructure marks a significant step towards redefining the future of urban mobility," said Amel Chadli, Gulf Cluster and Countries President at Schneider Electric."The vertiport at Dubai International Airport, VDX, reflects Dubai's position as a global leader in adopting the technologies that will define the next generation of transport.

As Skyports' energy technology partner, our role is to provide the energy and digital infrastructure that enables safe, reliable and efficient operations from day one, with an architecture built to scale as the network expands across the city."

source_snapshot.title: Dubai Municipality introduces smart navigation system with audio for visually impaired people
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Dubai Municipality has become the first government entity in the UAE to introduce NaviLens, a smart navigation system that helps people who are visually impaired find their way around public spaces and access information independently, the civic body revealed on Monday.The technology is among the highlights Dubai Municipality is showcasing at the eighth edition of AccessAbilities Expo, running from October 19 to 21, 2026, at Dubai World Trade Centre.It appears alongside accessible beaches, sensory rooms, a workplace inclusion programme and a new partnership with the Emirates Down Syndrome Association..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..How NaviLens worksNaviLens uses digitally encoded coloured markers that can be detected through smartphone cameras, giving users immediate audio and text-based guidance.The system supports more than 35 languages, making navigation and information services accessible to a wider range of people.Dubai Municipality says the move reflects its efforts to adopt assistive technologies that address different accessibility needs and improve the experience of using public facilities..Bader Anwahi, CEO of the Public Facilities Agency at Dubai Municipality, said: "Universal accessibility is a fundamental consideration in how we plan, develop and manage Dubai's public facilities. Our responsibility extends beyond providing accessible infrastructure to ensuring that public spaces and services respond to the different needs of the people who use them. This requires an integrated approach that brings together inclusive design, assistive technologies and the continuous improvement of facilities and services."Beaches and sensory roomsBeach accessibility is another focus of the Municipality's stand. Its accessible beach infrastructure includes sea swimming platforms at Jumeirah Beach 2 and Khor Al Mamzar, along with 10 accessible entrances and pathways to the sea, dedicated parking spaces for People of Determination across all beaches and 16 accessible restrooms.Floating wheelchairs for swimming and specialised beach wheelchairs are also available, helping People of Determination enjoy Dubai's coastal destinations safely and independently.The Municipality is also showcasing its sensory rooms across Dubai's parks and beaches, including a dedicated facility at Jumeirah Beach 2.Designed to accommodate different sensory needs, these spaces offer supportive environments that enhance comfort, wellbeing and the overall visitor experience.The accessibility enhancements at Jumeirah Beach 2 have also earned the destination the Gold Classification from the World Disability Union (WDU), recognising its inclusive facilities for People of Determination..Inclusion at work and in the communityAt the expo, Dubai Municipality is marking the graduation of the first and second cohorts of its Inclusion Coordinators Programme. The programme equips participants with the knowledge and practical skills needed to support the inclusion of People of Determination in the workplace, promotes greater awareness of accessibility requirements and helps create an environment where they can participate effectively and develop professionally.Community members are being encouraged to play a part too, through the Municipality's 'Access Ambassadors' initiative. It raises awareness of universal accessibility requirements under the Dubai Building Code and guides People of Determination and building owners towards the Municipality's 'Wusool' service. It also gives residents a chance to propose ideas and practical solutions to accessibility challenges.The Municipality is further showcasing emergency evacuation and safety systems designed to accommodate the needs of People of Determination, supporting safer evacuation procedures in buildings and public facilities.New partnership and global recognitionOn the sidelines of AccessAbilities Expo 2026, Dubai Municipality signed a cooperation agreement with the Emirates Down Syndrome Association to strengthen collaboration on universal accessibility and the inclusion of People of Determination.The agreement will support efforts to enhance accessibility and inclusive design across the Municipality's facilities, services, programmes and communication channels. It will also provide a framework for joint sports, recreational, cultural and community initiatives for People of Determination and their families.A key part of the cooperation will involve drawing on the Association's specialised expertise and the experiences of People of Determination to evaluate accessibility solutions, test services and identify opportunities for improvement.Dubai Municipality's accessibility achievements also include a Guinness World Record, received in 2023, for the world's longest Braille handrail at Dubai Frame, measuring 319 metres and 11 centimetres. Its own stand at this year's expo, which features wide tactile pathways and accessible facilities, has received a Certificate of Achievement for its inclusive design.Anwahi added: "AccessAbilities Expo provides an important opportunity to exchange expertise, engage with People of Determination and strengthen collaboration with organisations working to advance universal accessibility. We recognise that developing an inclusive urban environment requires ongoing engagement, practical solutions and a clear understanding of users' experiences. Through these partnerships and initiatives, we aim to continue raising accessibility standards across Dubai's public facilities and contribute to the Emirate's position as a city friendly to People of Determination.".Watch: Dubai's Jumeirah Beach 2 turns 'Gold' with a sensory room. What's it?.Dubai Frame, Children's City and these Dubai parks are now officially special. source_snapshot.title: A new high for adventure seekers as Bungee at Yas Bay opens on Yas Island
source_snapshot.text: ABU DHABI, 19th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Adventure seekers now have a brand-new reason to visit Yas Island as Bungee at Yas Bay officially opens at Yas Bay Waterfront on Nov 1,2026. Launching from a 50-metre platform overlooking the waterfront, the new attraction delivers a thrilling experience that combines breathtaking views, adrenaline-fuelled excitement and an unforgettable challenge, adding another must-try experience to Yas Island's growing portfolio of world-class attractions.Whether guests are looking to push their limits, tick off a bucket-list experience or simply see Yas Bay Waterfront from a completely new perspective, Bungee at Yas Bay offers an exhilarating journey from start to finish. Operated by Warrior Group and designed to the highest safety standards, the attraction combines the excitement of a controlled free-fall with spectacular waterfront views, creating a memorable experience for first-time jumpers and adrenaline enthusiasts alike.Jonathan Brown, Chief Portfolio Officer, Miral, said: “The opening of Bungee at Yas Bay adds an exhilarating new dimension to Yas Island’s expanding portfolio of world-class experiences. It reflects our ongoing efforts to create joyful and unforgettable moments for our guests, while reinforcing Yas Island’s position as a leading global destination for entertainment and leisure.”“We are delighted to partner with Miral to bring this new adventure experience to Yas Bay. At Warrior Group, we are passionate about creating experiences that bring people together, inspire them to try something new and add value to the destinations we design, build and operate in. The Bungee at Yas Bay is an exciting addition to Abu Dhabi’s leisure offering. With its spectacular waterfront setting and views, this new attraction offers residents and visitors a unique opportunity to experience Yas Bay from a whole new perspective,” Troy Gillham, Founder and CEO, Warrior Group.The experience is open to guests aged 16 and above, with a permitted weight range of 40–105kg. A professional crew will prepare guests for the leap with a safety briefing and equipment checks before each jump. Participation is subject to health and eligibility requirements, with full details available at https://abu-dhabi.platinumlist.net/event-tickets/bungee-at-yas-bay.

source_snapshot.title: UAE school photo ban: Parents and educators back children’s privacy safeguards
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Parents taking photographs or videos of children on school premises without consent could face fines of up to Dh500,000 under UAE privacy laws if a complaint is raised with the authorities and the conduct is found to constitute an offence, legal experts have said.The clarification comes after schools in Dubai and Sharjah issued circulars asking parents and visitors not to photograph or film students on campus, or share images containing other children through WhatsApp groups, social media or other digital platforms without appropriate consent.While photographs help families preserve memories of school performances, celebrations and other milestones, educators say children’s privacy and dignity must remain a priority, particularly when images can be circulated beyond their intended audience..Nevita Pandya MBE, CEO and Principal of GEMS International School – Dubai Hills, believes clear guidelines help children participate in school life without feeling pressured to have their images captured or shared.She explains, "Children should be able to participate fully in school life without their images being captured or circulated without appropriate permission." As she adds, a photograph can reveal more than we realise, including a child’s school, location or routine. "Clear guidelines establish that children’s privacy and dignity come before an adult’s wish to record or share a moment.”She adds that schools and parents should also consider children’s own preferences. “Alongside parental permission, we should listen to children’s views in an age-appropriate way and respect their discomfort. Their participation in school life should never depend on agreeing to publicity.”.Why sharing school photographs can be riskyEven when photographs are shared in familiar WhatsApp groups, parents may have little control over where the images go next.“It is essential. A familiar WhatsApp group can feel private, but images can still be saved, forwarded or shared beyond the intended audience,” Pandya says.Before sharing a photograph, she advises parents to consider whose children are visible, whether permission covers that use and whether the image reveals personal information. “Permission to take a photograph should not be assumed to include permission to publish it.”Dr Ghadeer Abu-Shamat, Principal of Al Khaleej International School, says children’s images should be treated with the same care as other personal information."Once an image is shared, especially online, it can be difficult to control who has access to it or how it may be used in the future. Being mindful helps protect children's safety, dignity, and privacy.”.She adds that knowing photographs of her child are not circulated without her knowledge gives families greater peace of mind.“It gives families greater control over their child's digital footprint and reduces the risk of images being viewed, copied, or shared beyond the intended audience. It also demonstrates respect for parental choice and children's privacy rights.”.Parents call for a balance between privacy and sharing memoriesWhile supporting safeguards around children's images, parent Suad Saleh, whose child attends GEMS International School, believes the rules should encourage responsible behaviour rather than prevent families from sharing every photograph.“If it’s a photo of your own children, with no other children visible in the background, and it’s an appropriate and respectful photo, I don’t necessarily see any harm in sharing it. I think the important thing is also to be mindful of who you are sharing it with and the privacy of your children.”For Saleh, “it’s about using good judgment rather than saying that parents should never photograph or share pictures of their children.”She believes the guidelines should focus on educating parents about responsible sharing.“I think that the rules should emphasise more to educate and encourage responsible behaviour rather than simply restrict parents completely.”Dr Abu-Shamat says the rules can encourage parents to consider the consequences before posting or forwarding images.“These rules encourage parents to pause and consider the implications before posting or forwarding images. They reinforce the importance of consent, respect for other families, and awareness of digital safety.”Simon Jodrell, Principal of Jebel Ali School in Dubai, says clear guidance can help parents understand how to share photographs responsibly, even when their intentions are good.“Often, parents share photographs with the very best intentions, without necessarily considering who else might appear in the background or where those images might eventually end up,” he says. “Simple, sensible guidance encourages parents to think before posting and to respect the wishes of others.”.Teaching children about consent and online responsibilityThe guidelines could also help children develop healthier attitudes towards privacy and sharing images online, particularly when parents model the behaviour they expect from their children.“Asking before taking or sharing a photograph teaches children that their boundaries matter and that other people’s boundaries deserve equal respect,” Pandya says.She also points to wider digital wellbeing concerns, including appearance-based comparison, the pursuit of online approval, and social media use that displaces sleep or physical activity.“Effects vary, but those risks deserve serious attention. We should help young people understand that their worth is not measured by likes, and that meaningful experiences do not always need to be photographed, posted or publicly validated.”Saleh agrees that rules alone are not enough. Children also need to see adults respecting other people's boundaries. “When children see their parents asking permission, respecting boundaries, and being thoughtful about what they share, they learn that digital responsibility is part of everyday life.”Jodrell believes the guidelines can also open up conversations at home about children’s digital footprints and their right to privacy.“Children are growing up in a world where sharing photographs and information is part of everyday life, so it is important they understand that not everything needs to be shared publicly,” he says.He advises parents to ask children how they feel about having their photographs shared, model considerate behaviour and explain why other people’s privacy matters. Schools can reinforce these lessons through teaching about responsible online behaviour.Dr Abu-Shamat says the guidelines provide an opportunity for families to discuss consent, digital citizenship, privacy and online responsibility, helping children understand that not every moment needs to be photographed or shared..How parents can support schoolsSchools can help families understand the rules by explaining when photography is permitted, what consent covers and how images may be shared, Pandya says.As she says, families should understand that permission concerning their own child does not extend to other children. School-managed photographs, shared through appropriately restricted channels and in accordance with consent, can help families preserve memories while limiting exposure.She adds that children whose families decline photography must remain fully included in school celebrations.“We should also encourage adults to be present and enjoy the occasion. Celebrating achievement and belonging should never require a child to surrender their privacy.”Parents can support schools by following photography and filming policies, seeking permission before photographing or sharing images of other children, and respecting families who do not consent.Dr Abu-Shamat also advises parents to avoid sharing school-related photographs in WhatsApp groups or on social media if other students are identifiable, without the necessary consent. Saleh recommends avoiding sensitive personal information when sharing images.

They reinforce the importance of consent, respect for other families, and awareness of digital safety.”Simon Jodrell, Principal of Jebel Ali School in Dubai, says clear guidance can help parents understand how to share photographs responsibly, even when their intentions are good.“Often, parents share photographs with the very best intentions, without necessarily considering who else might appear in the background or where those images might eventually end up,” he says.

“Simple, sensible guidance encourages parents to think before posting and to respect the wishes of others.”.Teaching children about consent and online responsibilityThe guidelines could also help children develop healthier attitudes towards privacy and sharing images online, particularly when parents model the behaviour they expect from their children.“Asking before taking or sharing a photograph teaches children that their boundaries matter and that other people’s boundaries deserve equal respect,” Pandya says.She also points to wider digital wellbeing concerns, including appearance-based comparison, the pursuit of online approval, and social media use that displaces sleep or physical activity.“Effects vary, but those risks deserve serious attention.

We should help young people understand that their worth is not measured by likes, and that meaningful experiences do not always need to be photographed, posted or publicly validated.”Saleh agrees that rules alone are not enough.
Children also need to see adults respecting other people's boundaries.

“When children see their parents asking permission, respecting boundaries, and being thoughtful about what they share, they learn that digital responsibility is part of everyday life.”Jodrell believes the guidelines can also open up conversations at home about children’s digital footprints and their right to privacy.“Children are growing up in a world where sharing photographs and information is part of everyday life, so it is important they understand that not everything needs to be shared publicly,” he says.He advises parents to ask children how they feel about having their photographs shared, model considerate behaviour and explain why other people’s privacy matters.

Schools can reinforce these lessons through teaching about responsible online behaviour.Dr Abu-Shamat says the guidelines provide an opportunity for families to discuss consent, digital citizenship, privacy and online responsibility, helping children understand that not every moment needs to be photographed or shared..How parents can support schoolsSchools can help families understand the rules by explaining when photography is permitted, what consent covers and how images may be shared, Pandya says.As she says, families should understand that permission concerning their own child does not extend to other children.

School-managed photographs, shared through appropriately restricted channels and in accordance with consent, can help families preserve memories while limiting exposure.She adds that children whose families decline photography must remain fully included in school celebrations.“We should also encourage adults to be present and enjoy the occasion.

Celebrating achievement and belonging should never require a child to surrender their privacy.”Parents can support schools by following photography and filming policies, seeking permission before photographing or sharing images of other children, and respecting families who do not consent.Dr Abu-Shamat also advises parents to avoid sharing school-related photographs in WhatsApp groups or on social media if other students are identifiable, without the necessary consent.
Saleh recommends avoiding sensitive personal information when sharing images.

source_snapshot.title: UAE bans use of popular antibiotic for pets and farm animals from November 1
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: The UAE is banning the use of ciprofloxacin, a popular antibiotic, in its veterinary sector from November 1, 2026, in a move aimed at tackling antimicrobial resistance.The Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) on Tuesday announced that the ban covers veterinary medicinal products and raw materials containing ciprofloxacin.It affects nine veterinary products, including eight imported products and one locally registered product.Ciprofloxacin belongs to the fluoroquinolone group of antibiotics. It is a strong antibiotic used to treat certain bacterial infections..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..Why the ban?The decision is part of efforts to promote the safe use of antibiotics and preserve the effectiveness of treatments used in human medicine. It follows the classification of this group of antibiotics as Critically Important Antimicrobials (CIAs) for human medicine because of their role in treating certain bacterial infections.Inappropriate use in animals could contribute to the development of bacterial resistance, potentially reducing the effectiveness of available treatments and posing a public health challenge.The ban follows a scientific assessment of data related to antimicrobial resistance, including studies submitted by UAE University. The findings were used to support evidence-based regulatory decisions and strengthen national efforts to reduce the risks associated with antimicrobial resistance..Risk-based approachDr Ruqaya Aqeel Al Bastaki, Acting Executive Director of the Medical Products Regulation Sector at the Emirates Drug Establishment, said regulating the use of antimicrobials requires an approach based on assessing the risks associated with each substance and how those risks affect treatment priorities across different sectors.She explained that scientific evidence plays a key role in determining the appropriate level of regulatory intervention, allowing the establishment to take necessary measures when findings point to risks that require action, taking into account the nature of each substance and its uses.Al Bastaki added that the establishment is committed to keeping its decisions aligned with the latest scientific developments and responding proactively to risks linked to antimicrobial resistance. . These efforts aim to preserve the effectiveness of available treatments, strengthen pharmaceutical security, ensure the sustainability of medical products and protect public health.The decision falls within the Emirates Drug Establishment's mandate to regulate the use of medical and pharmaceutical products and monitor compliance with the relevant approved requirements.What companies must doAhead of the ban's implementation, the establishment has taken the necessary regulatory steps to identify the products and raw materials covered by the decision.It has notified the relevant establishments that they must stop manufacturing, importing and supplying these products, withdraw existing quantities from the local market before the ban takes effect, and either re-export or dispose of remaining stocks in accordance with approved procedures.Establishments must also submit supporting documents confirming that the required measures have been completed.EDE is also preparing a monitoring plan to assess compliance with the decision and verify that the relevant establishments complete the required procedures within the specified timeframe.The decision was taken as part of the Emirates Drug Establishment's efforts to strengthen oversight of veterinary medical products, promote the responsible use of antimicrobials and support national initiatives to combat antimicrobial resistance, helping protect human and animal health while strengthening the UAE's public health system, EDE said..UAE recalls two 'Goodbye All Insects' insecticide products.UAE announces new mechanism to end monopoly of medicines.FNC calls for lower drug prices, publication of banned medicines .UAE enacts law to regulate veterinary medicines and enhance food safety

source_snapshot.title: Sharjah introduces motorcycle parking for first time in Al Yarmook
source_snapshot.text: Sharjah: Sharjah has rolled out dedicated motorcycle parking in Al Yarmook for the first time, alongside 4,160 paid parking spaces, 53 roads and new recreational facilities as part of a major infrastructure upgrade.Sharjah City Municipality has completed the project to upgrade roads, pavements and parking facilities in the area in seven and a half months, ahead of the original one-year contractual deadline. The development was carried out under the directives of His Highness Sheikh Dr Sultan bin Mohammed Al Qasimi, Supreme Council Member and Ruler of Sharjah.Covering 185,000 square metres, the project aims to improve residents’ quality of life, ease movement around the neighbourhood, enhance road safety and give Al Yarmook a more organised urban appearance..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..The improvements also include a new 5,400 square metre park, 280 newly planted trees, 227 energy-efficient streetlights, 32 pedestrian benches and an integrated camera surveillance system.Dedicated motorcycle parking introducedFor the first time across Sharjah, dedicated motorcycle parking spaces have been introduced as part of the Al Yarmook development project, providing designated areas for riders and helping improve parking management across the emirate.The initiative forms part of a wider effort to organise parking, reduce random parking and make it easier for residents and visitors to find designated spaces.The project also created and prepared 4,160 paid parking spaces along roadsides and in internal open areas. The spaces are intended to improve vehicle parking arrangements and make more efficient use of available land.53 roads and improved infrastructureThe project covered a total area of 185,000 square metres and included the construction of 53 roads covering 56,876 square metres, with a combined length of approximately nine kilometres.It also involved the development and maintenance of the internal road network, as well as 41 lanes, passages and pedestrian pavements covering more than 31,320 square metres.Infrastructure works included electricity, water and gas lines, telecommunications networks, sewage systems and rainwater drainage facilities. The project also focused on organising utility routes, improving connectivity between buildings and public facilities, and making movement through the neighbourhood easier for residents and visitors.Sewage and rainwater drainage works have been completed in full, covering 14,800 linear metres.Quality control measures included reviewing detailed network plans, checking the quality of construction materials, monitoring implementation, testing the networks, verifying levels and inspecting rainwater inlets, manholes and associated structures.The municipality also cleaned and levelled 36 plots of land covering approximately 31,000 square metres. Some of these plots were earmarked for smart parking facilities, while others were designated for school buses.The work has improved the appearance of the neighbourhood while allowing better use of available land..New parks and more green spacesThe municipality has expanded recreational facilities in Al Yarmook with the development of a 5,400 square metre park featuring a shaded children's play area, a football pitch, visitor seating and an office for security and park supervision.A second, smaller park was also created, with its design incorporating an existing mature ghaf tree to preserve it. The park includes a children's play area and family seating, providing an additional community space for residents.The municipality also planted 280 sea hibiscus trees, alongside other flowering species, along the main roads to enhance Al Yarmook’s urban landscape and expand its green spaces. The project also included maintaining existing landscaped areas to preserve greenery and improve the neighbourhood’s overall appearance.Free permits for building façade improvementsImproving the appearance of buildings was another key part of the development.Engineer Faisal Al Mulla, Director of the General Services Department at Sharjah City Municipality and head of the project team, said the municipality established a specialised team to monitor building façades alongside the main construction team.The initiative covered more than 535 buildings, and maintenance permits were issued for 231 of them.All permits issued to property owners for modifying or maintaining building façades were provided free of charge, easing the process of repainting buildings and removing features that detract from the area's overall appearance.The initiative is intended to improve the urban landscape while preserving the neighbourhood's aesthetic character.Dedicated centre for municipal inspectorsUnder the directives of the Ruler of Sharjah, a plot of land was allocated for a dedicated building to serve as a base for municipal inspectors carrying out field duties in the area.The facility has been completed and fully equipped in accordance with the required specifications and standards.Inspectors will use the centre as a starting point for monitoring public cleanliness, the area's overall appearance, building façades, shop signs and other signage, as well as carrying out other duties within their responsibilities..227 streetlights and surveillance camerasThe project included the installation of 227 energy efficient streetlights and 32 benches along pedestrian pavements to improve safety and comfort for residents and visitors.An integrated camera surveillance system was also established to strengthen security and safety throughout the area.Project completed ahead of scheduleAl Mulla said the project was completed in seven and a half months through advance planning, coordinated implementation and cooperation among the government entities involved.Although the original contractual period was one year, the work was organised according to an ambitious eight months schedule to minimise disruption and complete the improvements as quickly as possible.The neighbourhood was divided into seven work zones, allowing construction to proceed in phases while keeping parts of the area accessible to residents and shop owners. This approach helped avoid a complete closure of the neighbourhood and reduced the impact of construction on daily life and business activity.The project was carried out in collaboration with the Sharjah Roads and Transport Authority, the Department of Planning and Survey, the Directorate of Public Works, Sharjah Police General Command, and the Sharjah Electricity, Water and Gas Authority.The Roads and Transport Authority was involved from the early stages, reviewing the works, monitoring implementation and overseeing quality to ensure compliance with approved technical specifications and standards.The project began with the approval of infrastructure plans and the issuance of the required certificates and permits, followed by the implementation and inspection of the works.The municipality said the improvements are intended to provide an integrated, safe and sustainable urban environment, improve access throughout Al Yarmook and enhance the daily experience of residents and visitors. Sharjah Al Yarmook project: Key factsDirective: Implemented under the directives of His Highness Sheikh Dr Sultan bin Mohammed Al Qasimi, Ruler of Sharjah. Area: 185,000sqm; completed in 7.5 months, ahead of the one-year deadline.Roads: 53 roads spanning 56,876sqm and approximately 9km.Parking: 4,160 paid spaces; dedicated motorcycle parking introduced for the first time across the areas covered.Pedestrian facilities: 41 lanes, passages and pavements covering 31,320sqm.Infrastructure: 14,800 linear metres of sewage and rainwater drainage networks completed.Land: 36 plots covering 31,000sqm cleaned and levelled for smart parking and school buses.Parks: One 5,400sqm park and a smaller park preserving a mature ghaf tree.Greenery: 280 trees planted; existing landscaped areas maintained.Building façades: 535-plus buildings covered; 231 free maintenance permits issued.Lighting and seating: 227 energy efficient streetlights and 32 benches installed.Security: Integrated CCTV surveillance system established.Municipal services: Dedicated, fully equipped base for municipal inspectors.Construction: Seven work zones to minimise disruption to residents and businesses.Partners: Roads and Transport Authority, Planning and Survey, Public Works, Sharjah Police, and Sharjah Electricity, Water and Gas Authority. .Sharjah's Dh500 million drainage project reaches 70 per cent completion.Sharjah launches Dh750m road project to ease Dubai commute, first opening due in November 2026.Sharjah opens Al Khan Park in record time ahead of Eid Al Adha.Sharjah expands smart parking network with 2,421 AI-powered spaces

source_snapshot.title: Dubai sets new speed limits on five roads under traffic safety drive
source_snapshot.text: Dubai's traffic authorities are reducing the speed limits on three roads and increasing them on two others, as part of the Dubai Traffic Safety Strategy. The changes have been authorised by the emirate's Roads and Transport Authority and Dubai Police. The speed limit has been raised from 60kph to 70kph on Al Mustaqbal Street, between Sheikh Rashid Street and Al Meydan Street, and on Latifa bint Hamdan Street, between Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road. On Al Asayel Street, between Oud Metha Street and Al Meydan Street, the limit will be increased from 60kph to 80kph. The limit on Al Rebat Street, between Marrakech Street and Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Road, will be reduced from 100kph to 90kph, and from 80kph to 70kph on Sheikh Sabah Al Ahmad Al Jaber Al Sabah Street, between 2nd December Street and Khalid bin Al Waleed Street. The changes will come into effect from November 1 and are in line with a major drive by Dubai transport authorities to boost road safety and improve traffic flow to keep pace with the needs of a growing population.

source_snapshot.text: Dubai: The Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure has invited engineering consultancy firms to bid for the study and design of the Fourth Federal Highway Corridor (E-911), a proposed 68-kilometre road linking the Dubai-Sharjah border to Ras Al Khaimah.The ministry said in a post on X that only Category A consultancy firms are eligible to apply for the contract, which covers engineering studies, design and optional supervision services..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..Tender No. 2026-022 was issued on October 15, with interested firms required to submit their bids by Friday, October 23.According to details published on the ministry's website, the proposed highway will extend from the Dubai-Sharjah border to Al Shuhada Road in Ras Al Khaimah.The project also includes an eight-kilometre connecting road linking the new corridor to Emirates Road (E-611) in Umm Al Quwain.The highway will feature between 12 and 16 lanes in both directions combined, with the number of lanes varying along different sections of the route.The tender represents a step towards developing the project, with consultants expected to undertake the technical studies and engineering designs required before construction.The ministry has not disclosed the project's estimated construction cost or implementation timetable.Dubai's 80km Fourth Corridor projectThe tender comes a month after Dubai announced a separate 80-kilometre Fourth Corridor project in September, aimed at strengthening the emirate's road network and improving connectivity between Sharjah, Dubai and Abu Dhabi.The first phase, estimated to cost Dh3.5 billion, will extend from Al Shanouf Road in Sharjah to Dubai-Al Ain Road. The second phase will continue from Dubai-Al Ain Road to Al Faya Road in Abu Dhabi.While the federal E-911 project will provide a new road connection between the Dubai-Sharjah border and Ras Al Khaimah, Dubai's Fourth Corridor project is designed to improve transport links towards Abu Dhabi.Both developments are intended to expand road capacity and strengthen connectivity between the emirates..Dubai’s new 80km road project explained: Route, traffic cuts and what’s being built.Dubai's Dh750 million Emirates Road project reaches 30 per cent completion, cutting journey times by 65 per cent.Dubai approves 80km Fourth Corridor to cut travel time.How a Dh6 billion highway will change travel in the UAE

source_snapshot.title: Dubai tenants warned: Read rental contracts carefully
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Signing a tenancy contract without reading the fine print could land tenants and landlords in costly legal disputes, Dubai’s Rental Disputes Center (RDC) has warned.The centre has urged residents and business owners to carefully review every clause of their rental agreements before signing, particularly those relating to rent payments, financial guarantees, contract renewal and eviction.The warning follows a number of rental disputes involving overlooked contractual conditions, undocumented agreements and verbal promises that were never formally recorded.MisunderstandingsAccording to the RDC, such misunderstandings can result in financial claims, compensation demands and even eviction proceedings.Highlighting the risks, the centre cited the case of a tenant who became involved in a legal dispute with his landlord just months after starting a commercial activity. The disagreement arose over payment arrangements and financial guarantees included in the tenancy contract.The tenant referred to separate arrangements made with the landlord. However, these had not been formally documented.As the dispute escalated, the written tenancy agreement became central to the case because it clearly outlined the obligations accepted by both parties.The RDC said the undocumented arrangements lacked sufficient supporting evidence before the relevant authority.Fine print mattersThe centre explained that many rental disputes arise not from deliberate wrongdoing but from tenants or landlords rushing to sign agreements without fully understanding their legal implications.It advised both parties to pay particular attention to payment deadlines, contractual penalties, eviction provisions and the conditions governing renewal or termination.Even a seemingly minor clause could have significant financial or legal consequences if a disagreement arises later.Ejari registrationThe RDC also reminded landlords and tenants of the importance of registering tenancy contracts through Dubai’s Ejari system.Registration provides an officially recognised record of the rental relationship and helps protect the rights of both parties.Failure to register a tenancy agreement may create procedural difficulties when seeking to enforce certain rights or obligations through official channels.The centre also advised landlords and tenants to retain copies of correspondence, notices and other documents relating to their rental arrangements.Any changes to the original agreement, including revised payment schedules or additional conditions, should be formally documented rather than left to verbal understandings.The RDC stressed that a successful rental relationship begins before a tenant receives the keys or starts occupying a property.What tenants should check before signing Rent payments: Confirm amounts, deadlines and payment arrangements.Financial guarantees: Understand deposits and other financial commitments.Renewal and termination: Check notice periods and relevant conditions.Penalties: Review any charges for breaching contractual terms.Ejari registration: Ensure the tenancy contract is officially registered.Additional agreements: Put any changes or special arrangements in writing..Dubai rental dispute process: How to file a case, fees, documents and what happens next.Dubai landlord refusing to return your security deposit? source_snapshot.title: UAEV, Dubai World Trade Centre sign agreement to expand EV charging infrastructure
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 21st October, 2026 (WAM) -- UAEV has signed an agreement with Dubai World Trade Centre (DWTC) to develop and deploy electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure across designated parking areas at the Dubai World Trade Centre and Dubai Exhibition Centre. Signed on the sidelines of WETEX, the agreement will expand access to charging at key business, exhibition and event destinations in Dubai.The planned infrastructure will serve visitors attending exhibitions, conferences and events, alongside businesses and commercial fleets operating in and around these locations. By integrating charging facilities into existing parking areas, the initiative aims to make charging more convenient and support the growing demand for electric mobility.Phase 1 of the deployment at DWTC will cover four locations, establishing the project’s initial footprint within one of Dubai’s busiest business and exhibition districts.Ali Al Darwish, Acting CEO of UAEV, said: “Access to charging is an important consideration for people and businesses choosing electric vehicles. Our agreement with DWTC will bring charging services closer to drivers at destinations they already use for work, business and events, making it easier to fit charging into their day.“As we expand our network, we are working with partners to integrate charging into locations that serve a wide range of users. This collaboration will help us meet the needs of individual drivers and commercial operators, while supporting the UAE’s transition to more sustainable mobility.”Abdulrahman Obaid Abu Al Shawareb, EVP of Protocol and Security at DWTC, said: “Dubai World Trade Centre continues to enhance its infrastructure in line with Dubai’s ambitions for a more sustainable and future-ready urban environment. Our collaboration with UAEV will enable us to progressively expand EV charging facilities across our destinations, enhancing the overall visitor experience by providing greater convenience and accessibility for our visitors, tenants, and stakeholders, while supporting the wider adoption of sustainable mobility in Dubai.”The agreement brings together UAEV’s charging expertise and DWTC’s exhibition and commercial destinations to support the continued expansion of Dubai’s public EV charging network. It reflects a shared commitment to developing infrastructure that responds to changing mobility needs and supports the UAE’s wider sustainability objectives.

source_snapshot.text: RTA Enhances Mahboub to Enable Integrated Services Using AI Assistants Upgrade Designed to Simplify Customer Journeys and Enable Easier Service Completion Through a Unified Conversational Experience Dubai. Roads and Transport Authority. 22 October 2026: Dubai’s Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) has upgraded Mahboub, its virtual assistant, using AI assistant technology to simplify the customer journey and facilitate the completion of RTA services through a unified conversational experience. The enhanced version is being prepared for public rollout as part of RTA’s Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2030. New Capability: Coordinating and Executing Procedures Mahboub uses AI assistants to coordinate and execute services involving interconnected steps, in addition to the information and services it currently provides. Depending on each customer’s request, the system activates specialised AI assistants to coordinate and carry out the required procedures, such as paying vehicle fines and then renewing vehicle registration, according to the customer’s needs. Simpler Customer Journeys and Targeted Impact The system enables customers to complete these procedures within a single conversation. The process includes using the UAE PASS digital identity for verification and the Dubai Sadad platform for payment. The initial scope focuses on vehicle licensing services, including vehicle registration renewal, vehicle fines payment, a clearance certificate issuance and number plate reservations renewal. Mahboub supports Arabic and English, with language models fine-tuned to suit the local context. Mahboub aims to reduce the need for customers to switch between pages and channels, as well as the number of steps required to complete transactions. It is also expected to reduce the time and effort involved in accessing services. Development is being carried out in accordance with RTA’s established governance and cybersecurity procedures. The enhancement reflects RTA’s drive to develop leading, customer-centric digital services and reinforce Dubai’s standing with the aim of establishing the emirate as a global leader in trusted, smart government services.

source_snapshot.title: Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure enhances federal road readiness for rainy season
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 22nd October, 2026 (WAM) -- The Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure continues its proactive preparations for the rainy season by enhancing the readiness of federal roads and associated facilities, conducting preventive inspections and maintenance of stormwater drainage networks, pumping stations, and culverts, and strengthening monitoring and field response capabilities.The efforts aim to ensure road user safety and maintain service continuity under various weather conditions.As part of its preparations, the Ministry is inspecting and maintaining stormwater drainage networks, clearing waterways where wadis intersect with federal roads, and ensuring the efficiency and operational readiness of 17 pumping stations and 800 stormwater drainage culverts.It is also deploying specialised field teams and providing the necessary equipment and machinery to address water accumulation and various weather conditions, enabling faster response times, safer roads, and uninterrupted traffic flow.The Ministry continues to carry out preventive inspections and maintenance, including assessing structural conditions, removing sediment, and ensuring the operational readiness of discharge gates, waterways, and monitoring systems. These measures strengthen the infrastructure's capacity to accommodate rainwater flows and mitigate the risks of flash floods and flooding.It operates a smart, around-the-clock monitoring system for dams and wadis, equipped with surveillance cameras and sensors that measure water levels and flow rates. The system includes an early flood warning mechanism connected to the control centre and relevant national authorities, helping anticipate potential risks, issue alerts, and support proactive measures to protect lives and property.In addition, the Ministry continues to coordinate with its federal and local partners to strengthen joint preparedness, review emergency plans, and enhance field response procedures. This collaboration ensures the rapid exchange of information, coordinated responsibilities, and effective management of various rainfall scenarios, while minimising their impact on lives, property, and infrastructure.The Ministry continuously monitors the federal road network through its control centre, which provides real-time oversight of road conditions and field developments.The centre supports timely decision-making and the deployment of emergency and maintenance teams to affected locations in coordination with relevant authorities. This enables a rapid response to rainwater accumulation, minimises traffic disruptions, and enhances road user safety and service continuity.Eng. Mohammed Al Mansoori, Undersecretary for Infrastructure and Transport Affairs at the Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure, said that protecting lives and property and ensuring the continuity of essential services are key priorities in the Ministry's plans. He noted that preparations for the rainy season begin well in advance, with assessments of federal roads, dams, and water infrastructure, the identification of priority locations, and enhanced field team capabilities to respond effectively to various weather conditions.He said, "We follow a proactive approach focused on enhancing infrastructure readiness and strengthening its resilience to changing weather conditions, with particular emphasis on rapid response and minimising the impact of rainfall on traffic flow. We are committed to developing an integrated operational system that combines preventive maintenance, continuous monitoring, and coordinated field response to ensure road user safety and service continuity."Al Mansoori added, "Our investments in infrastructure development go beyond improving operational efficiency. They also focus on strengthening resilience and adaptability to different climatic conditions, ensuring that our infrastructure meets future development needs while maintaining the quality of services provided to the community."

source_snapshot.title: UAE end-of-service gratuity: How much are employees entitled to and when must it be paid?
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Private sector employees in the UAE are entitled to end-of-service gratuity based on their basic salary and length of service, with employers required to settle all outstanding payments within 14 days of the termination of their employment contracts, according to the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MoHRE).In an awareness post explaining key provisions of the UAE Labour Law, the ministry outlined how gratuity is calculated, eligibility requirements and the deadlines employers must follow when settling employees' financial entitlements..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..Under the law, expatriate employees who complete at least one year of continuous service are entitled to end-of-service gratuity calculated on their last basic salary.Employees receive the equivalent of 21 days' basic salary for each year of service during their first five years of employment. For every additional year of service beyond the first five years, the entitlement increases to 30 days' basic salary.The ministry clarified that employees who have completed at least one continuous year of service are also entitled to gratuity for any additional partial year, calculated proportionately according to the period worked.However, the total gratuity payable must not exceed the equivalent of two years' wages, regardless of the employee's length of service.14-day payment deadlineMoHRE stressed that employers must pay all end-of-service entitlements and outstanding wages within 14 days from the date an employee's contract ends.The requirement is intended to ensure that workers receive their financial entitlements promptly following the termination of their employment.The ministry also highlighted its voluntary Savings Scheme, which provides an alternative mechanism for managing and growing employees' end-of-service benefits.Under the scheme, employers can participate in approved investment funds, allowing employees' end-of-service benefits to be invested and potentially generate returns over time.The ministry said the initiative provides an opportunity to strengthen employees' financial security while supporting more sustainable management of end-of-service entitlements.The clarification forms part of MoHRE's efforts to raise awareness of labour rights and obligations, helping employees understand their financial entitlements and employers comply with the UAE Labour Law..UAE gratuity calculation: What happens if your basic salary is reduced?.UAE gratuity: When can your employer legally deduct from your end-of-service benefits?.UAE gratuity guide: How to calculate your final settlement.Is UAE gratuity calculated on basic salary or gross salary?

source_snapshot.title: Google, YouTube expand online child safety drive with US$2.4 million Google.org funding, Dubai child safety Pop-up
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 23rd October, 2026 (WAM) -- Google.org is supporting INJAZ Al-Arab with US$2.4 million in funding to empower youth across the Middle East and North Africa region with digital safety and online citizenship training over four-years through Google’s Arabic-language Abtal Al Internet (Be Internet Awesome) curriculum.The initiative aims to reach over 2.3 million young people across nine countries including the United Arab Emirates, Egypt, Morocco, Tunisia and Saudi Arabia.First launched in Arabic in 2018, Abtal Al Internet is Google’s digital literacy programme for children between the ages of seven and thirteen. The grant marks Google’s latest contribution to online safety in the region.The announcement coincides with the launch of the Google Abtal Al Internet Pop-Up Playground at Alserkal Avenue in Dubai, in partnership with the UAE Telecommunications and Digital Government Regulatory Authority (TDRA) and the National Media Authority (NMA).The Pop-up, which is open to the public between 24-25 October, offers families an engaging, hands-on experience of Google’s digital literacy programme Abtal Al Internet and the parental control features available on Google products, including YouTube Kid and Teen accounts and the stand-alone YouTube Kids app.Abdulla bin Mohammed bin Butti Al Hamed, Chairman of the National Media Authority, said creating a safe digital environment for youth is a strategic pillar of the UAE's vision to build a secure and sustainable knowledge-based society that protects future generations from online risks while empowering them to harness digital opportunities responsibly and consciously.He said the Authority is working to raise digital awareness and promote responsible use of online platforms, ensuring that technology serves as a tool for knowledge, creativity and progress.Speaking during a visit to Google’s “Be Internet Awesome” interactive space (Abtal Al Internet), Al Hamed stressed the importance of digital literacy in helping children distinguish reliable information from misinformation, protect their privacy and interact respectfully online.He added that preparing future generations goes beyond mastering technological tools, requiring a set of values and skills that enable children to use technology consciously and responsibly. He noted that increased digital awareness broadens opportunities for exploration and creativity, empowering youth to help build a safer and more beneficial digital environment.“Whether seeing a life-sized T-Rex with Augmented Reality on Search, exploring biology with AbdulAllah Anan on YouTube, or using Gemini’s Study Notebook to prepare for a chemistry quiz, kids use our products every day to make sense of the world. As parents and leaders, our job is to help them navigate these spaces safely, building healthy habits and becoming responsible digital citizens,” said Anthony Nakache, Managing Director, Google MENA.Google builds protections directly into its products, combining default safeguards for under-18 accounts, such as private uploads, turned-off autoplay, and disabled personalised ads, with controls like Google Family Link and the YouTube Family Centre.Across MENA, more and more families are turning to YouTube to learn real life skills. Research by Kantar found that 95% of viewers in Saudi Arabia and the UAE believe YouTube offers leading educational content, while 92% of Gen Z respondents said the platform has helped them develop new skills.Eng. Saeed Belhoul, Acting Director-General of the TDRA, said, “TDRA’s child digital safety strategy is based on an integrated approach that combines prevention, awareness, and empowerment, while reinforcing shared responsibility among families, relevant entities, and digital platforms. As technology and artificial intelligence continue to evolve rapidly, we believe that protecting children does not necessarily mean avoiding their engagement with the digital world, but rather empowering them to explore it and benefit from its opportunities with awareness, confidence, and responsibility, while building a generation equipped with the knowledge and skills to make informed and safe decisions in the digital environment.”"We want parents to feel empowered when their children open YouTube to learn and explore, whether they are building a science experiment at home or diving into the region’s rich history. By pairing strong default protections with easy-to-use parental controls, every unique family can customise their experience and make the most of YouTube's educational content," said Javid Aslanov, Head of YouTube MENA.Earlier this year, YouTube launched Kid & Teen Accounts to give parents across the Middle East and North Africa additional content controls based on their child’s stage of development, including an industry-first Shorts feed timer to manage viewing, with the option to set it to zero minutes per day. In 2021, YouTube launched its stand-alone kids app, YouTube Kids offering robust parental controls.Healthy digital habits take ongoing conversation. To help families start open discussions about screen time and online safety at home, Google and YouTube created a simple Family Online Safety Agreement that parents and kids can adapt together:● Talk openly about what we watch, play, and share online.● Keep personal details private (like passwords, addresses, and phone numbers).● Double-check facts before sharing links or stories.● Choose kindness online and report toxic behavior.● Agree on trusted adults to talk to whenever something feels uncomfortable or confusing.

The grant marks Google’s latest contribution to online safety in the region.The announcement coincides with the launch of the Google Abtal Al Internet Pop-Up Playground at Alserkal Avenue in Dubai, in partnership with the UAE Telecommunications and Digital Government Regulatory Authority (TDRA) and the National Media Authority (NMA).The Pop-up, which is open to the public between 24-25 October, offers families an engaging, hands-on experience of Google’s digital literacy programme Abtal Al Internet and the parental control features available on Google products, including YouTube Kid and Teen accounts and the stand-alone YouTube Kids app.Abdulla bin Mohammed bin Butti Al Hamed, Chairman of the National Media Authority, said creating a safe digital environment for youth is a strategic pillar of the UAE's vision to build a secure and sustainable knowledge-based society that protects future generations from online risks while empowering them to harness digital opportunities responsibly and consciously.He said the Authority is working to raise digital awareness and promote responsible use of online platforms, ensuring that technology serves as a tool for knowledge, creativity and progress.Speaking during a visit to Google’s “Be Internet Awesome” interactive space (Abtal Al Internet), Al Hamed stressed the importance of digital literacy in helping children distinguish reliable information from misinformation, protect their privacy and interact respectfully online.He added that preparing future generations goes beyond mastering technological tools, requiring a set of values and skills that enable children to use technology consciously and responsibly.

He noted that increased digital awareness broadens opportunities for exploration and creativity, empowering youth to help build a safer and more beneficial digital environment.“Whether seeing a life-sized T-Rex with Augmented Reality on Search, exploring biology with AbdulAllah Anan on YouTube, or using Gemini’s Study Notebook to prepare for a chemistry quiz, kids use our products every day to make sense of the world.

As parents and leaders, our job is to help them navigate these spaces safely, building healthy habits and becoming responsible digital citizens,” said Anthony Nakache, Managing Director, Google MENA.Google builds protections directly into its products, combining default safeguards for under-18 accounts, such as private uploads, turned-off autoplay, and disabled personalised ads, with controls like Google Family Link and the YouTube Family Centre.Across MENA, more and more families are turning to YouTube to learn real life skills.

Research by Kantar found that 95% of viewers in Saudi Arabia and the UAE believe YouTube offers leading educational content, while 92% of Gen Z respondents said the platform has helped them develop new skills.Eng.

Saeed Belhoul, Acting Director-General of the TDRA, said, “TDRA’s child digital safety strategy is based on an integrated approach that combines prevention, awareness, and empowerment, while reinforcing shared responsibility among families, relevant entities, and digital platforms.

As technology and artificial intelligence continue to evolve rapidly, we believe that protecting children does not necessarily mean avoiding their engagement with the digital world, but rather empowering them to explore it and benefit from its opportunities with awareness, confidence, and responsibility, while building a generation equipped with the knowledge and skills to make informed and safe decisions in the digital environment.”"We want parents to feel empowered when their children open YouTube to learn and explore, whether they are building a science experiment at home or diving into the region’s rich history.

By pairing strong default protections with easy-to-use parental controls, every unique family can customise their experience and make the most of YouTube's educational content," said Javid Aslanov, Head of YouTube MENA.Earlier this year, YouTube launched Kid & Teen Accounts to give parents across the Middle East and North Africa additional content controls based on their child’s stage of development, including an industry-first Shorts feed timer to manage viewing, with the option to set it to zero minutes per day.
In 2021, YouTube launched its stand-alone kids app, YouTube Kids offering robust parental controls.Healthy digital habits take ongoing conversation.

To help families start open discussions about screen time and online safety at home, Google and YouTube created a simple Family Online Safety Agreement that parents and kids can adapt together:● Talk openly about what we watch, play, and share online.● Keep personal details private (like passwords, addresses, and phone numbers).● Double-check facts before sharing links or stories.● Choose kindness online and report toxic behavior.● Agree on trusted adults to talk to whenever something feels uncomfortable or confusing.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai Future Solutions – Prototypes for Humanity summit to showcase 100 innovative projects from leading universities worldwide
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 23rd October, 2026 (WAM) -- The annual Dubai Future Solutions – Prototypes for Humanity summit returns to Dubai from 18 to 21 November 2026. Held under the patronage and leadership of H.H. Sheikha Latifa bint Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Chairperson of Dubai Culture and Arts Authority (Dubai Culture), the summit brings together one of the world’s largest and most diverse communities of academic innovators and provides a platform for turning research into real-world impact.This year’s edition will take place on The Prototype Floor during Dubai Future Week, held under the patronage of H.H. Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence of the UAE, and Chairman of the Board of Trustees of Dubai Future Foundation. The Week will run from 18 to 21 November 2026 at Emirates Towers and the Museum of the Future, under the theme ‘For the Human of the Future’.Organised by Dubai Future Foundation, Dubai Future Week is expected to bring together more than 10,000 participants from around the world, including experts, innovators, investors, policymakers and entrepreneurs. The programme will feature talks, policy discussions, investment pitches, competitions and public experiences exploring how emerging technologies can shape the future.Held as part of the summit, the Dubai Future Solutions – Prototypes for Humanity exhibition will feature 100 innovative projects selected from thousands of submissions by academics representing around 1,000 universities across more than 120 countries. Five outstanding projects, one in each of the initiative's five main categories, will be honoured during the event.Organised annually by Art Dubai Group in partnership with Dubai Future Foundation, Dubai International Financial Centre and the Hussain Sajwani – DAMAC Foundation, the initiative brings together leading innovators, researchers, professors, students and graduates from universities worldwide. It provides a platform to exchange knowledge and expertise, showcase academic research and explore how innovative ideas can be transformed into practical solutions to some of humanity's most pressing social, economic and environmental challenges.Dubai Future Solutions – Prototypes for Humanity aims to support university innovators from around the world in developing their ideas into practical applications. The exhibition also gives the public an opportunity to explore a wide range of research-driven solutions across healthcare, agriculture, water, energy, transport, the environment and civil society.This year's cohort includes teams from more than 70 universities across 33 countries, representing some of the world's leading academic institutions. These include Harvard University, Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), the University of Oxford, the University of Cambridge, ETH Zurich, Imperial College London, Cornell University, the National University of Singapore and Delft University of Technology.The exhibition will also feature teams from universities in emerging economies, including Ghana, Peru, Morocco and Chile, alongside academic institutions from the UAE, including New York University Abu Dhabi, Khalifa University of Science and Technology and the American University of Sharjah.Khalfan Juma Belhoul, CEO of Dubai Future Foundation, said: “Dubai Future Solutions – Prototypes for Humanity reflects Dubai's vision of supporting creative minds and empowering future generations to develop innovative solutions to global challenges.”He added: “The initiative's objectives also align with Dubai Future Week and its theme, ‘For the Human of the Future’. It has become a global platform that brings together leading researchers and innovators from universities and academic institutions worldwide, enabling them to showcase their ideas and transform their research into practical projects that make a positive difference to communities.”Hussain Sajwani, Founder of DAMAC Group, said: “Dubai embodies an extraordinary vision for the future, driven by the ambition of its wise leadership and its proactive approach to transforming bold visions into tangible achievements. This is achieved through investments in innovation and technology, and the adoption of solutions that place people at the heart of development, with the aim of building a more competitive and sustainable economy.”He added: "Dubai Future Solutions - Prototypes for Humanity" reflects this vision, reaffirming that shaping the future is not about waiting for it to unfold, but about anticipating it and taking proactive steps to plan for it. At DAMAC, we believe our responsibility lies in translating this vision into transformative projects and strategic investments that contribute to urban development, enhance quality of life, and harness innovation for the benefit of humanity. Through these efforts, we aim to further strengthen Dubai’s position as a global hub for shaping the future, while creating a positive and lasting impact for generations to come.”This year's projects reflect a world adapting to rapid change, as innovators respond to rising temperatures, growing pressure on natural resources and the rapid adoption of artificial intelligence in everyday life.Beyond software, algorithms and data systems, teams are developing physical devices and robotic systems, biotechnology and bio-based solutions, advanced materials and chemical formulations. They are also redesigning industrial and environmental processes and exploring new ways to generate, store and convert energy.In healthcare, innovators are developing solutions to enable earlier diagnosis, improve the delivery of care and make healthcare more accessible.Among the featured projects, HEURIS helps emergency department clinicians consider the full range of possible diagnoses as test results become available. Age Resist uses a wearable device to analyse sweat composition and assess the body's ability to withstand and recover from physical stress associated with surgery. ChronoVasc, meanwhile, estimates the biological age of a person's arteries through a single blood test.Projects focused on climate and natural resources are developing innovative ways to use energy and materials more efficiently while transforming waste into valuable resources.SolarSkin enables solar panels to switch automatically between generating electricity and heating indoor spaces. MetCycle dissolves materials from spent batteries in less than 15 minutes at room temperature, while AlgaePalm produces an alternative to palm oil using UAE microalgae cultivated in saltwater.Other projects demonstrate how data and artificial intelligence can support smarter cities and strengthen public trust.Greenery Scanner monitors the health of street trees and maps their condition using cameras installed on vehicles travelling through city streets. Coco: Heat Minimizer helps people identify cooler walking routes during heatwaves, while Litmus independently assesses whether companies are fulfilling their commitments to protecting user privacy.Dubai Future Solutions – Prototypes for Humanity also supports academic entrepreneurs through a dedicated venture-building programme that provides funding, business expertise and specialised support, alongside opportunities for direct collaboration with industry partners. The programme helps participating teams transform scientific research into practical solutions that address real industry needs.The programme begins by testing the feasibility of selected technologies in real-world environments, before supporting participants in establishing companies, developing their businesses and expanding their operations.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai Police warn of Dh400 jaywalking fine as part of road safety campaign
source_snapshot.text: Dubai Police have warned pedestrians of crossing roads unsafely, reminding them of a fine of Dh400. According to Article 89 of the Federal Traffic Law, pedestrians who disregard traffic signals or cross roads at undesignated locations can be fined Dh400. Brigadier Majid Sultan Al Suwaidi, Director of the General Department of Police Stations, urged pedestrians to use designated crossings, check that the road is clear of approaching vehicles and obey pedestrian traffic signals at intersections. “Road safety is a shared responsibility. Everyone has a role to play in following traffic regulations and helping create safer roads for all,” he said. The reminder comes as the authority launched an awareness campaign to promote pedestrian safety, encourage responsible road behaviour and reduce traffic accidents. The campaign also targets motorists, reminding them to remain vigilant, reduce speed and give way to pedestrians at designated crossings, particularly in busy and densely populated areas.

source_snapshot.title: Pakistani expats in UAE: E-Passports start, fees from Dh145
source_snapshot.text: The Embassy of Pakistan in Abu Dhabi and the Consulate General of Pakistan in Dubai have begun processing all passport applications as e-Passports from Friday, October 23, 2026, according to a public notice issued by the missions. The notice said the e-Passport issuance process “has started and will continue”, covering all new applications submitted at both offices. Pakistani nationals holding valid Machine Readable Passports (MRPs) do not need to replace them immediately. The missions said all valid MRPs remain valid until their date of expiry. Applicants have been advised to apply for renewal only when the remaining validity of their passport is less than six months. The notice also said that both a first name and a last name are mandatory for the e-Passport. Applicants whose current passports carry only a single name should be prepared for this requirement when applying. Over two million Pakistanis live in the UAE, making them the country’s second-largest expatriate community in the country. The community includes professionals, entrepreneurs and workers across various industries, with many considering the Emirates a second home after years or generations of residence. Beyond contributing to the UAE’s development, Pakistanis play a vital role in supporting their home country through remittances. Fees vary by the number of pages, validity period, processing type and whether the passport is being replaced after loss. All fees are in UAE dirhams.For a standard renewal, the lowest fee is Dh145 for a 36-page, five-year passport under normal processing, while the same document with a 10-year validity costs Dh215. A 72-page passport costs Dh260 for five years and Dh390 for 10 years under normal processing. Urgent processing adds a premium across all categories. Fees also rise sharply for replacements, with a second loss of a 72-page passport under urgent processing costing Dh1,700 for five years and Dh2,540 for 10 years. https://t.co/1Ls4GyVpPv pic.twitter.com/dCPxG0ppcR — Pakistan Embassy UAE (@PakinUAE_) October 23, 2026

source_snapshot.title: St. Regis Dubai, The Palm to reopen on November 1 after 6 months of refurbishment
source_snapshot.text: The St. Regis Dubai, The Palm will reopen its doors on November 1, 2026. The announcement by St. Regis Hotels & Resorts on Friday, marks the return of one of Palm Jumeirah's most well-recognised hotels. The hotel was temporarily closed for a major refurbishment in the middle of April this year. source_snapshot.title: Ras Al Khaimah closes all beaches 'until further notice'
source_snapshot.text: Ras Al Khaimah closed all its beaches "until further notice", according to a notice by the emirate's Public Services Department. Earlier, the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment confirmed an oil spill off Umm Al Quwain to be the source of the 'fuel-like' smell that residents reported across multiple emirates. All beaches and coastal areas in Umm Al Quwain have been temporarily closed until teams complete assessments, and identify safety and marine protection measures, the ministry said. The odours "pose no health risk" to residents, the ministry confirmed. After the spill was detected, teams immediately began containment, cordoning, cleanup and remediation to limit environmental impact, Moccae said.
