source_snapshot.title: Public Art Abu Dhabi Biennial begins second edition in Al Ain
source_snapshot.text: AL AIN, 24th October, 2026 (WAM) -- The second edition of the Public Art Abu Dhabi Biennial, organised by the Department of Culture and Tourism – Abu Dhabi (DCT Abu Dhabi), opened yesterday in Al Ain. Presented under the theme Home: A Glossary for a Communal Sense of Place, the Al Ain chapter brings four newly commissioned works to Al Qattara Oasis, part of the UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape of Al Ain, and to Al Towayya Roundabout, placing contemporary art within working farms, historic irrigation networks and the everyday routes of the city. The Al Ain works remain on view until 15 February 2027, with the Biennial opening across Abu Dhabi on 15 November 2026.Under the artistic direction of Elvira Dyangani Ose, Artistic Director of Zeitz Museum of Contemporary Art Africa (MOCAA), the second edition approaches the concept of ‘home’ as an evolving, collective and plural condition rather than a static geographic site. Through distributed commissions, research-led practices and public encounters, the Biennial prioritises sustained engagement, inviting audiences to interact with art in their everyday spaces. The title proposes that what communities share in relation to Abu Dhabi is not the place itself, but the capacity to construct meaning in relation to it, through the diverse vocabularies, practices and forms of knowledge that the glossary is designed to hold.At Al Qattara Oasis, Moroccan artist M'barek Bouhchichi presents ‘I am not the stone thrown into the water, but the seed sown in the field’ (2026), a stainless-steel work that reimagines the pigeon tower, a vernacular architecture found from North Africa to the Emirates, as a space of refuge and passage. Taking its title from Tayeb Salih’s Season of Migration to the North, the work carries a poem from Al Nahma, the traditional Emirati sea shanties sung by sailors, rendered in Braille across its structures. Nearby, Indian artist Reena Saini Kallat’s Thresholds: Requiem (The Last Call) (2026) reimagines twentieth-century acoustic locators, once designed to detect distant aircraft, as vessels for the calls of extinct and critically endangered bird species, several of which are native to, or migrate through, the UAE and the Arabian Peninsula. Spanish artist Asunción Molinos Gordo’s Bil Hana wa Al Afia (2026) centres on Al Aflaj, the traditional irrigation systems that originated during the Iron Age and continue to support shared water distribution among farmers in the Emirates. Built from rammed-earth walls arranged in a root-like form, its seven stratigraphic layers incorporate pottery, artefacts and other material traces from different historical periods, set among the working farms of the oasis.At Al Towayya Roundabout, Emirati artist Roudhah Al Mazrouei, born in Al Ain, presents Tassa (2026), an 80-metre-diameter sculpture that reimagines the traditional Emirati gold headpiece as a monumental public landscape. Drawing on heirloom jewellery passed down through generations, the work transforms its cascading chains, curved forms and ornamental details into an immersive environment. Developed through conversations and workshops with children, Tassa proposes heritage as something lived, shared and continually reimagined.Elvira Dyangani Ose, Artistic Director, Public Art Abu Dhabi Biennial 2026–27, said: “What do we mean when we say home? It is one of the most used terms in any language, and yet many aspects of it often go unexamined. Home is not only a location. It is a condition: felt before it is understood, carried in the body before it is articulated in language. Al Ain is where this edition begins, in an oasis landscape shaped over millennia by cooperation, shared water and collective care. We offer this Biennial as a glossary, not as a guide to correct interpretations but as a set of terms to think with. The definitions are partial by design, and yours to complete.”The Al Ain chapter inaugurates the Biennial’s second edition, which continues across Abu Dhabi from 15 November 2026 with further commissions, research-led projects and a public programme, details of which will be announced in the coming weeks. The second edition builds on the inaugural Public Art Abu Dhabi Biennial, Public Matter (2024–25), which presented site-specific commissions by artists from the UAE and around the world. Several works from the first edition have since been acquired or retained as long-term installations, contributing to the emirate’s growing public art collection.The Public Art Abu Dhabi Biennial is on view in Al Ain from 23 October 2026 to 15 February 2027 and in Abu Dhabi from 15 November 2026 to 15 February 2027.

source_snapshot.title: Dh60,000, 4.4kg and built like a camera: Rare Batman comic on display in Sharjah
source_snapshot.text: A Batman comic book that weighs 4.4kg, comes with a detachable lens and is designed to resemble a camera is on display at the Sharjah Animation and Comics Conference (SACC), with a price tag of Dh60,000. Only 47 copies of Batman: The Killing Joke Avant-Garde Edition are being produced worldwide. The handcrafted collector’s edition is being exhibited at the Argent Comics booth at the event, which runs until Sunday at Aljada. The book is inspired by the camera featured on the famous cover of Batman: The Killing Joke, originally published in 1988. Its aluminium boards are lined with goatskin, while the edition also features a detachable lens and a viewfinder. It is kept in a carrying case covered in calf leather and lined with suede. Croatian publishing imprint Argent Comics developed the edition under the direction of its creative director Marko Matijašević. According to the publisher, it is the world’s first giclée-printed comic book. The pages are printed on specially made Hahnemühle metallic paper using a patent-pending process. Vibor Kreća, a Croatian exhibitor representing Argent Comics at SACC, said making the book involves painstaking manual work. “You have to print on each side and then fuse them together by hand,” he said. The 47-copy run is also deliberate. Kreća said the number reflects silver’s atomic number, linking it to the Argent brand, whose name is associated with the metal. The edition contains two versions of the artwork from the acclaimed Batman story, written by Alan Moore and illustrated by Brian Bolland. Readers can see John Higgins’ original colouring as well as Bolland’s 2008 recolouring. Kreća said Bolland had been unhappy with the earlier coloured version of the book and later revisited it. “This is like a director’s cut,” he said. The collector’s edition also includes a transparent film negative, Bolland’s signature, a new introduction by the artist and additional material. At the booth, visitors can also see a black-and-white Noir edition of The Killing Joke. Inspired by the Joker’s prison cell, it features aluminium doors, a two-colour goatskin binding and letterpress-printed cotton paper. “This is cotton paper, which is letterpress, so you can feel everything. It’s very tactile,” said Kreća. Organised by the Sharjah Book Authority, the fourth edition of SACC features more than 150 activities and over 75 speakers from more than 30 countries. Its programme includes workshops, panel discussions, film screenings, live performances and exhibitions focused on animation and comics.

source_snapshot.title: 40 million students, Dh11m in prizes: Arab Reading Challenge to crown winner on Oct 29
source_snapshot.text: The Arab Reading Challenge will crown the winners of its tenth edition on October 29, 2026, at a closing ceremony at the Dubai World Trade Centre. Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President and Prime Minister of the UAE and Ruler of Dubai, said the country remains committed to serving the Arabic language and nurturing new generations who believe that progress begins with reading and knowledge. "The future of a nation begins with nurturing its young minds. Our investment in the Reading Challenge is an investment in a better future for all," he said. "For centuries, the Arabic language served as the driving force for human and social progress. It will restore its former glory once again with the dedication and brilliant minds of its youth." Record participation Organised by the Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum Global Initiatives, this year's edition drew over 40 million students from 60 countries, including 74,062 in the People of Determination category. This massive participation marks a 24 per cent increase over the challenge’s ninth edition and represents 48 per cent of all school students across the Arab World. The challenge also involved 138,426 schools and 161,507 supervisors. Mohammad Al Gergawi, Secretary-General of the Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum Global Initiatives (MBRGI), which organises the challenge, described this year’s edition as a landmark: "The tenth edition is a major milestone for the Arab Reading Challenge, drawing a record-breaking participation of over 40 million students and expanding across 60 countries for the first time," he said. "This remarkable reach reflects the deep appreciation and support the initiative commands across the Arab world and beyond." The closing ceremony will crown: Arab Reading Challenge Champion: Dh500,000 (second: Dh100,000; third: Dh70,000) People of Determination Champion: Dh200,000 (second: Dh100,000; third: Dh50,000) Best School: Dh1 million (second: Dh500,000; third: Dh300,000) Outstanding Supervisor: Dh300,000 (second: Dh100,000; third: Dh50,000) Community Champion: Dh200,000 total (first: Dh100,000; second: Dh70,000; third: Dh30,000) — open to students outside the Arab world, non-native Arabic speakers and those learning Arabic as a second language Total prizes awarded since the challenge launched now stand at Dh110 million, with Dh11 million given to winners each year. A growing challenge Launched in 2015 by Sheikh Mohammed as the largest-ever Arab literacy initiative, the Arab Reading Challenge has grown dramatically. Participation in the tenth edition is up 1,019 per cent compared with the first, which drew 3.6 million students. Last year, the ninth edition brought together 32.231 million students from 50 countries. The main title went to Tunisian twins Bisan and Baylasan Kouka, while Maria Hassan Ajil from Iraq won the People of Determination category. The challenge aims to promote reading among students across the Arab world and beyond, strengthen language skills, and nurture a lasting love of knowledge and the Arabic language.

source_snapshot.title: RTA completes World Trade Centre Roundabout Development Project, to open final bridge October 30
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 25th October, 2026 (WAM) -- Dubai’s Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) will open the final bridge of the World Trade Centre Roundabout Development Project this Friday, 30th October 2026. The 1,000-metre, two-lane bridge will accommodate approximately 3,000 vehicles per hour, serving traffic from Al Majlis Street towards 2nd December Street.The bridge will improve traffic flow at one of Dubai’s key intersections, cutting journey time from Al Majlis Street to 2nd December Street from six minutes to one minute.With its opening, RTA will have completed all major works under the World Trade Centre Roundabout Development Project, which include five bridges with a combined length of 5,000 metres, at a cost exceeding AED696 million.Mattar Al Tayer, Director-General, Chairman of the Board of Executive Directors of RTA, said the project involves converting the former roundabout into an at-grade intersection, improving traffic flow on Sheikh Zayed Road and enhancing connectivity between the emirate’s leading economic and commercial centres. It will also reduce average delay at the intersection from 12 minutes to 90 seconds, benefiting more than 500,000 residents and visitors.Al Tayer explained that the World Trade Centre Roundabout Development Project complements Al Mustaqbal Street Development Project, scheduled for completion in 2027. The project includes bridges and tunnels spanning a total of 1,500 metres and expansion of the street to four lanes in each direction, increasing its capacity by 33 percent.The World Trade Centre Roundabout Development Project includes a bridge at the second level towards Deira, two bridges linking Sheikh Rashid Street with 2nd December Street, and another two bridges connecting Al Majlis Street with 2nd December Street, providing free-flowing traffic in multiple directions.The integrated project serves key areas, including Dubai World Trade Centre, Dubai International Financial Centre, Zaa’beel, Al Satwa, Al Karama, Al Jafiliya and Al Mankhool.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai Municipality awards AED3 billion worth of contracts for four projects under Phase 3 of ‘Tasreef’ Programme
source_snapshot.text: DUBAI, 25th October, 2026 (WAM) -- In line with the directives of His Highness Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Vice President and Prime Minister and Ruler of Dubai, to develop advanced, resilient and world-leading infrastructure and enhance the efficiency of the stormwater drainage system to meet the emirate’s future growth requirements, Dubai Municipality has awarded contracts for four new projects under Phase 3 of the ‘Tasreef’ Programme to develop Dubai’s stormwater drainage network. With a total value of AED3 billion, the projects will involve the construction and extension of approximately 100 kilometres of main stormwater drainage lines, with diameters of up to 3 metres, further enhancing the resilience of the city’s drainage network.The new projects are distributed across vital areas representing key economic, commercial, industrial and tourism corridors across the emirate, covering nearly 100 square kilometres. They include the development of stormwater drainage systems and networks in Jumeirah, Umm Suqeim, Al Safa, Al Manara, Al Quoz, Al Barsha, Al Wasl, Za’abeel, Al Bada’a, Al Satwa and Al Marmoom, connecting these areas to Dubai Municipality’s main stormwater drainage network. The projects will increase the network’s water-flow capacity, enhance operational resilience and support sustainable urban growth.The third package of projects represents an integrated extension of the Tasreef Programme, one of the UAE’s largest strategic and transformational infrastructure projects. The programme is classified as the largest integrated stormwater collection programme in a single system in the region and one of the most operationally efficient. Implemented by Dubai Municipality at a total cost of AED30 billion, it will provide a highly resilient and advanced drainage system capable of meeting Dubai’s future requirements.The programme will enhance the city’s readiness and preparedness to address climate-related changes, increase stormwater drainage capacity by 700 percent, and reduce costs associated with the construction of pumping stations and operations and maintenance by 20 percent. It will also extend the lifespan of the network and support the objectives of the Dubai 2040 Urban Master Plan and the UAE’s Net Zero 2050 Strategy.Eng. Marwan Ahmed bin Ghalita, Director-General of Dubai Municipality, said, “Dubai Municipality continues to implement the phases of the ‘Tasreef’ Programme, one of Dubai’s largest strategic infrastructure projects, enhancing its efficiency and resilience, making it more sustainable and strengthening its ability to address both future climate change and accommodate population and urban growth.Our objective is to build a comprehensive and integrated model for a leading future city, characterised by a sustainable urban system and advanced infrastructure that serve people, enhance their quality of life and well-being, and strengthen their safety and security. At the same time, it provides a stable and enabling environment for the growth of businesses and economic, commercial and tourism activities, reinforcing Dubai’s position as the world’s best city to live, work, invest and visit.”Eng. Adel Mohammed Al Marzouqi, CEO of the Waste and Sewerage Agency at Dubai Municipality, said, “The third phase of the Tasreef Programme’s projects will serve areas that represent vital arteries across the emirate, marking another pivotal step in developing Dubai’s stormwater drainage system as well as making it more resilient and efficient in managing rainfall under different conditions and future climate changes. We are committed to ensuring that these projects advance the broader objectives of the Tasreef Programme by reducing water accumulation, protecting residents and assets, improving the quality of services, enhancing the city’s readiness and traffic flow, and safeguarding the sustainability of its resources.”The Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim Stormwater Drainage Network Development Project is one of the largest projects under the third phase of Tasreef. It aims to enhance infrastructure readiness along key strategic corridors across the two areas, serving communities extending from Umm Suqeim 1, 2 and 3, and Umm Al Sheif to Jumeirah 3, Al Safa 1 and 2, and Al Manara along the Dubai Water Canal.The project includes the construction of approximately 42 kilometres of main stormwater drainage lines, enhancing the resilience, efficiency and capacity of the drainage system.The Stormwater Drainage Network Development and Capacity Enhancement Project between Sheikh Zayed Road and Al Khail Road focuses on developing resilient and sustainable infrastructure capable of accommodating residential and urban growth and enhancing the city’s readiness and resilience.The project includes the construction of 14 kilometres of main stormwater drainage lines in accordance with the highest international standards.It will serve several of Dubai’s key strategic corridors and vital areas, including the Al Khail Road interchange towards Umm Suqeim, Umm Suqeim Road and Sheikh Zayed Road, in addition to First Al Khail Street, Al Marabea Street, Al Waha Street, Al Zumurrud Street and the connecting secondary roads.The project will cover Al Quoz Industrial Areas 1, 3 and 4, as well as Al Barsha 1.The Development of Main Stormwater Drainage Lines along Al Wasl Road Project aims to serve areas east of the Dubai Water Canal, including Za’abeel 2, Al Wasl, Jumeirah 1 and 2, Al Bada’a, Al Satwa, and Dubai World Trade Centre 1 and 2, covering an area of up to 25 square kilometres.The project includes an integrated stormwater drainage network comprising main and secondary conveyance lines and associated infrastructure, with a total length of 21 kilometres. This will enable the drainage and management of large volumes of water flow with operational flexibility, helping to prevent water accumulation.As part of the third phase of the Tasreef Programme, Dubai Municipality will develop an integrated and sustainable stormwater drainage network in Al Marmoom, serving vital areas by implementing 23 kilometres of stormwater drainage infrastructure. This will ensure continuity of services and enhance the quality of the area’s urban infrastructure.Dubai Municipality continues to implement strategic projects in accordance with approved timelines and operational plans, reaffirming its commitment to developing an integrated and resilient drainage system that contributes to reducing the risks associated with water accumulation, enhancing the efficiency and sustainability of infrastructure, and strengthening Dubai’s readiness to respond effectively to climate change.These efforts further support Dubai’s ambition to be recognised globally for the quality of its infrastructure and public services.

source_snapshot.title: Dubai to close some E611 lanes, Al Maktoum airport tunnel amid autonomous taxi testing
source_snapshot.text: Dubai's transport authority announced the closures of a major road and tunnel on Sunday, October 25, amid autonomous taxi companies' testing operations. Three lanes of the Emirates Road (E611), opposite Al Maktoum International Airport, are set to be closed during the highway testing, the RTA revealed in its statement. Additionally, the entire Al Maktoum International Airport Tunnel will also be closed in both directions. The closures are set to take place from October 26 to 31, between 9am and 4pm. Motorists have been urged to plan their journeys in advance and follow directional signs to ensure smooth travel. Earlier this month, a senior UAE official said the country would have more than 10,000 autonomous taxis and delivery vans operating next year, with orders already placed for the vehicles as the country prepares to sharply scale up driverless transport. Both Abu Dhabi and Dubai have already begun commercial autonomous taxi operations. Abu Dhabi expanded Level 4 autonomous taxi services on Yas Island earlier this year, while Dubai launched commercial autonomous taxi services in areas including Umm Suqeim and Jumeirah. Abu Dhabi had previously become the first city in the Middle East and North Africa to begin commercial operations of fully driverless Level 4 vehicles, according to Abu Dhabi Mobility.

title: Dubai to close some E611 lanes, Al Maktoum airport tunnel amid autonomous taxi testing
summary_ru: 🚇 Временное закрытие дорог в Дубае из-за тестирования автономных такси 📅 С 26 по 31 октября с 9:00 до 16:00 будут закрыты три полосы на шоссе Emirates Road (E611) напротив аэропорта Аль-Мактум и полностью туннель аэропорта в обе стороны. 🧪 Водителей просят планировать маршруты заранее и следовать указателям для удобства передвижения во время тестов автономных такси.

newsroom_profile.mission: Давать русскоязычным жителям Дубая проверенные и полезные новости без шума и кликбейта.
newsroom_profile.goal: Сформировать устойчивое медиа в Telegram с контролем качества и прозрачной редактурой.

editor.reason: Новость о временном закрытии дорог в Дубае из-за тестирования автономных такси соответствует тематике транспорта и городской инфраструктуры.
